That is why Scripture asks for attentive eyes. He blesses his youngest son and seems disappointed, as if he had blessed one for the other. Esau, who had gone hunting, came, bringing what his father had ordered, and said: Father, eat as you wished. Isaac answers: Who are you? And Esau: I am Esau, your eldest son. Isaac insisted: Are you Esau? Who then is he who brought me food and I ate, and I blessed him and he remains blessed? Get angry with the deceiver? Get angry with the deceitful? Rather say: Why did he deceive me? Why did it frustrate me? Let's remove that blessing for his brother and let's go at a bad time. Does not the event cry out that everything was done in mystery, so that the older could serve the younger? Then he receives a similar blessing. But he added: You will be your brother's servant. For Esau had said: Have the blessings run out? Bless me too. Isaac said, if I have already made him your master, what am I going to give you? But he insisted: Bless me too, father! Thus he extorted him and received a very similar blessing from the dew of heaven and the fertility of the earth in all abundance. But he added at once: You will serve your brother. And so it will be for you until you shake off the yoke from your neck. What is that which was said, So it shall be until you shake off the yoke from your neck, but to show that those whom Esau represented are sinners, but so that they are able and free to change and join themselves to the brother?

5. Pay attention to the mystery. See how the Jew is the servant of the Christian. That is evident, it filled the globe, as you see. That's Jacob. But, so that you can see that this was said about the future, consider history and see that it was not fulfilled in both brothers: the elder will serve the younger. We read that Esau became very rich and began to reign in all his fullness, while Jacob had to feed other people's sheep. And when he decided to return and was afraid of his brother, as has just been read, he sent I don't know how many gifts of cattle and a servant to say: "These are your brother's gifts." He did not want to see him before appeasing him with gifts, and he saw him when Esau had already received the gifts. When Jacob came to him, he worshiped him from afar. How is it fulfilled that the older will serve the younger, when it seems that the younger worships the older? This was not fulfilled in history, so that it is understood to be said in the future. That's Jacob. The younger son received the primacy, and the older son, the people of the Jews, lost it. Behold, Jacob filled the earth, he conquered the people and the kingdoms. A Roman emperor, now Christian, ordered that the Jews not approach Jerusalem itself 5. Scattered throughout the world, they became guardians of our books 6. Like slaves, when they go to court with their master, they carry the codices behind him and remain seated at the doors, so the eldest son serves the youngest. 5. ludaei Cbristianorum serví.—Attendite mysterium. Ecce Iudaeus servus est Christiani. Et hoc manifestum est, et implevit otbem terrarum, sicut videtis, Iacob. Et ut noveritis quia de futur dicebantur ista, considérate ipsam historiam, et videte quia non sunt impleta in ipsis duobus, Maior serviet minori (ib., 25,23). Ditatus enim legitur Esau multum, et tegnare coepit in tota abundantia (ib., 36,7). Ule autem Iacob, ut pasceret oves alienas. Et cum coepisset rediré, et timere fratrem suum, sicut moda legebatur, mittit muñera nescio quanta pecorum, mittit et servum qui dicat, Ecce muñera fratris tui (ib., 32,18). Noluit eum videre, priusquam muneribus placaret; et postea illum acceptis muneribus vidit. Et cum ad eum Iacob venisset, adoravit eum a longe (ib., 33,3). Quomodo ergo, Maior serviet minori, quando minor videtur adorare maiorem? Sed ideo ista in historia non sunt impleta, ut intellegantur de futur dictate. Minor filius accepit primatum, et maior filius perdidit primatum. Ecce Iacob implevit terram, [57] tenuit gentes et regna. Iussit imperator Romanus, iam Christianus, ut ad ipsam Ierusalem non accesoent ludaei. And sparsi per orbem terrarum, facti sunt quasi custodes Librorum nostrorum. Quomodo servi, quando eunt in auditorium domini ipsorum, portant post illos codices, et foris sedent: sic factus est filius maior filio minori. Disbelieving disciple felt his scars. Why didn't he want to be touched, but because he said it in figure? That woman was the Church. Don't touch me means don't touch me carnally, but insofar as I am equal to the Father. As long as you do not understand that I am equal to the Father, do not touch me, for you do not touch me, but my flesh. In the course of his perfection Paul says: If before we knew Christ according to the flesh, we no longer know him. And also: the old has passed, everything is now new; and everything is from God. What does it mean: if we knew Christ according to the flesh, we no longer know Him? It means that, when we knew him carnally, we thought he was nothing but a man 7. But when his grace shone in us, we discovered the Word, equal to the Father. Jacob held on and struggled, wanting to fight with his carnal habit. But the other said: Release me carnally, since it is already day, so that you may be spiritually enlightened, that is, do not believe me to be a man. Let go of me, it's already morning. We understand “tomorrow” in the light of Truth and Wisdom, because it is in whom all things were made. You will have to enjoy it when this night passes, that is, the iniquity of this century. The morning will open when the Lord comes and we will see him as the angels see him. Well now we see through a mirror and in an enigma, but then face to face. Let us retain, therefore, brothers, the said sentence: let me go, come on, it is already morning. And what did Jacob say? No te talliter, nisi cum ascendit ad Patrem? Adhuc hic erat, palpavit scars discipulus qui non credebat. Quomodo ergo nolebat se tangí, nisi quia hoc imagine dictum est? Illa mulier Ecclesia erat: et hoc est, Noli me tangere, noli me carnaliter tangere; sed qualis sum, aequalis Patri. Noli me tangere: quia non me, sed carnem meam tangís. Dicit enim in evectione profectus sui Paulus, Et si noveramus secundum carnem Christum, sed nunc iam non novimus; et, Velera transierunt, ecce jacta sunt nova; omnia autem ex Deo (2 Cor 5, 16-18). Quid est, Et si noveramus secundum carnem Christum, sed nunc iam non novimus? Quia quando eum carnaliter noveramus, non putabamus nisi quia homo erat tantum: at vero postquam gratia eius illuxit nobis, intelleximus Verbum aequale Patri. Tenebat ergo, et luctabatur, quasi eum carnali habitu Iacob amplecti volens. Ule autem dicebat, Dimitte me; carnaliter: quia ecce iam mane est, ut spiritualiter illumineris: id est, Noli me putare hominem. Resign, quia iam mane est. Mane in luz veritatis intelleximus, et sapientiae, per quam facta sunt omnia.

Ipsa perfrueris, cum nox ista transierit, hoc est, iniquitas huius saeculi. Tune enim fiet mane, cum venerit Dominus, ut ita a nobis videatur, quemadmodum ab Angelis videtur. Quia nunc videmus per speculum in aenigmate, tune autem facie ad faciem (1 Cor 13:12). Teneamus ergo hoc, fratres, quod dictum est, Dimitte me, This phrase has autobiographical value. Remember the words of the Confessions (VII 19,25): "But then I judged differently, feeling from my Lord Jesus Christ only what can be felt from a man of extraordinary wisdom... But what a mystery those words contained: 'The Word became flesh', I could not even suspect it."

I will let go if you don't bless me. Because the Lord blesses us first through the flesh. The faithful know, when they receive it, that they are blessed by the flesh. And they know that they would not be blessed if that flesh had not been crucified for the life of the world. And why is he blessed? Because he prevailed with God, because he held fast, and persevered, and did not let what Adam lost get out of hand. Let us faithfully retain what we receive, so that we may deserve to be blessed. 8. The paralyzed part of Jacob means bad Christians, so that blessing and surrender occur in him. Jacob is blessed by those who live well, and limped by those who live badly. In the same man both things occur now. But someday reparation and distinction will be made. That is what the Church desires, when it says in the psalm: Judge me, O God, and discern my cause from unholy people. Because the Gospel says: if your foot offends you, cut it off and throw it away from you. It will be better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one foot than to go with two feet into eternal fire. Therefore, these evil ones must be separated at last. Now the Church is lame. One foot stands firmly, but the other is invalid. Pay attention, brothers, to the pagans. Sometimes they find good Christians who serve God, and they are amazed, they are attracted and they believe. But sometimes they see them living badly and say: «Look at the Christians! » These who live poorly correspond to the tendon of the thigh that was touched and has dried up. That quia iam mane est. Sed ille quid dixit, Non te dimittam, nisi me benedixeris? Quia per carnem nos prius benedicit Dominus. Norunt fideles quid accipiunt; quia per carnem benedicuntur; et sciunt quia non essent benedicti, nisi caro illa crucifixa daretur pro saeculi vita. Quomodo autem benedicitur? Quia praevaluit Deo, quia tenuit fortiter, et perseveravit, et de manibus non dimisit, quod amisit Adam. Teneamus ergo fideles quod accepimus, ut benedici mereamur. 8. Iacob et benedictus et claudicans.—Pars arida [59] Iacob Christianos malo significat; ut in ipso Iacob et benedictio sit, et claudicatio. Benedictus est ex parte bene vivostium, claudicat ex parte male vivostium. Sed adhuc in uno homine est utrumque: erit autem diremptio et discretio postea; quod optat in Psalmo Ecclesia, they say: ludica me, Deus, et discerne causam meam de gente non sancta (Ps 42,1). touch is the hand of the Lord that punishes and vivifies. Therefore, on the one hand it is blessed and on the other it is dried up. The Lord designated these who live badly in the Church, because that is why he wrote in the Gospel that, when the grass grew, the tares appeared, because when people begin to improve, they also begin to realize the bad ones. You know all this, since, thank God, it is made known to you. But now we must tolerate the tares until the end of the harvest, lest by uprooting the tares the wheat will also be uprooted with them. The time will come when the Church will be heard, when she says: Judge me, O God!, and discern my cause of unholy people, when the Lord comes in his clarity with his holy angels; All nations will gather before him, and he will separate them, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats; He will place the righteous on the right and the goats on the left; To them he will say: Come, you blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom; and to them he will say: Go into eternal fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels.

et vivificans. Ideo ex parte benedicitur, et ex parte arescit. These men live in Ecclesia otendit Dominus; Quia inde est quod sctiptum est in Gospel, quia cum crevisset herba, apparuerunt zizania: quia cum coeperint nomines proficere, tune incipiunt ill will feel. Veniet autem tempus ut exaudiatur Ecclesia dices, Iudica me, Deus, et discerne causam meam de gente non sancta: cum Dominus venerit in claritate sua cum Angelis sanctis, et colligentur ante eum omnes gentes, et segregabit eos, sicut pastor segregat oves ab haedis: et ponetur iusti ad dexteram, haedi autem ad sinistram: et illis dicetur, Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum; illis autem, Ite in ignem aeternum, qui praeparatus est diabolo et angelis eius (ib., 25,31-41).

Topic: The vocation of Moses (Ex 3). Date: 408-411? Location: Unknown. 1. When reading the holy readings we paid attention to what is written in the first ' that was recited to us, and we are going to try to briefly share with your holiness what the Lord deigns to suggest to us; lest, carnally understanding the divine mysteries, you not only do not advance, but go backwards. And the first thing that this reading presented to our consideration was that God appeared to Moses. But God does not deign to appear in his substance, as he is, except to those who are pure in heart. For thus it is written in the Gospel: Blessed are the merciful, for they will see God. If ever God wanted to appear to the bodily eyes of the saints, he did not appear in himself, but in a visible and sensitive creature, so that he could be felt with this flesh, or in a voice that sounded to the
EO QUOD APPARUIT DOMINUS MOYSI IN RUBO

CAPUT I. — 1. Quomodo Dcus Moysi apparuit.—Cum sanctae lectiones legerentur, in ea quae scripta sunt in prima lectione, quae nobis recitata est, animo intendimus, et ea quae Dominus suggerit, breviter cum vestra Sanctitate participare curamus: ne carnaliter accipiientes divina mysteria, non solum non proficiatis, sed etiam deficiatis. Occurrit enim primo aspectibus nostris ex illa lectione divina, quod Deus apparuit Moysi. Apparere autem per substantiam suam, sicuti est, nonnisi mundis cordibus digntur. Sic enim scriptum est in Gospel: Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt (Mt 5,8). Oculis autem corporalibus sanctorum si quando Deus [60] voluit apparere, non per se ipsum, sed per creature visibilem atque sensibilem, quantum ista carne felt potest, apparuit; vel per vocem sonantem auribus, vel per ignem oculis, vel per In the ordinary liturgical celebration, the number of readings was usually three. A first, taken from the prophets (better, from the Old Testament) or from the Apostle (Saint Paul, generally), which was followed by the singing of a responsorial psalm. In conclusion, the Gospel. In the major festivities, the readings were already established by custom. In the remaining days, the bishop or, ultimately, the reader could choose one or the other, according to his interests or whim. The sermon also focused on what the preacher considered most interesting; very often, on the verse of a psalm. See F. VAN DER MEER, Saint Augustine, Shepherd of Souls p.498ss,

ears, or already in the fire to the eyes, or through an angel appearing in some visible form, although representing God 2. Let us understand, brothers, that this is how God appeared to Moses. For that Majesty who made heaven and earth, who rules the universe and the world, to whom the angels are always united, who contemplate his beauty with a clear mind, could not appear to the mortal eyes of men except by taking some visible and sensible creature corresponding to these visible eyes of the body: the same Wisdom of God, by whom all things were made, would not have appeared to human eyes if he had not taken mortal flesh. 2. Just as the Word of God, that is, the son of God, took flesh to appear before the eyes, so God, to appear to the eyes of men, always deigned to appear in some visible creature. You see very clearly in the Acts of the Apostles that an angel appeared to Moses in the bush. Is this creature true and that one false? Or is that one true and this one false? What to say? If we are Christians, if we believe well, both are true. And if both are true, how is it said here that God appeared and that an angel appeared there? Because the spirit, which, when speaking in the Acts of the Apostles, says that an angel appeared, explains in that reading how God appeared. That statement is the exposure of this darkness. So that you do not believe that God appeared by himself, it is explained to you how God appeared through an angelic creature. Why do you marvel when, when an angel appears, it is said: angelum in aliqua visibili specie apparentem, sed personam Dei gestantem. Sic intellegimus, fratres, appamisse Moysi Deum. Non enim maiestas illa, quae fecit caelum et tertam, et quae regit universum mundum, cui semper inhaerent Angelí contemplando eius pulchtitudinem puris mentibus, oculis mortalibus hominis potuit apparere, nisi assumpta visibili et sensibili cteatura, quae ad istos oculos visibiles cotporis pertinet: quandoquidem et ipsa Sapientia Dei, per quem facta sunt omnia, humanis oculis non appareret, nisi humanom catnem assumeret. CAPUT II.—2. Moysi Deus per angelum apparuit.—Quomodo etgo Verbum Dei, id est, Filius Dei, ut appareret oculis, carnem assumpsit; sic semper Deus, ut appareret oculis hominum, in aliqua creatura visibili apparere dignified est. Nam apertissime habes in Actibus Apostolorum, quia angelus apparuit Moysi in rubo (Act 7,30).

Numquid ist Scriptura vera, et illa false est? aut illa vera, et is ista false est? Be quid? Si christiani sumus, si bene credimus; ambae sunt verae. Si ergo ambae sunt verae, quomodo hic Deus apparuit, quomodo ibi angelus dicitur apparuisse, nisi quia ille Spiritus, qui in Actibus Apostolorum dixit apparuisse angelum, exposuit hanc lectionem quomodo apparuit Deus? Illa declaratio, expositio est obscuritatis huius: ne intellegeres Deum per se ipsum apparuisse,
See supplementary note 18: The Theophantases, p.749,
Moses' calling

God said, or also: Did God call Moses, and as he approached the place he repeated: Did God say to Moses? Because in the angel the temple is not cared for, but rather the one who lives in the angel. The angel himself was the temple of God. If He deigns to dwell and speak in a man, so that when a prophet speaks we say, "God said through Isaiah," how much more through an angel? When we say, “God said through Isaiah,” what is Isaiah? Was he not a man who carried his flesh, born of father and mother, like all of us? However, he speaks and what do we say about his words? "This is what the Lord says." What is God like if Isaiah speaks, but because God speaks through Isaiah? So here, when the angel speaks, it is said that God speaks. Why, if not because God speaks through the angel? 3. With that problem resolved, pay attention now to that reality in whose sign the appearance seems to be verified: it is a bush, and the bush was not burning, it was not catching fire; It seemed like fire, but it did not burn the bush. Do we think that the bush will mean something good when it has thorns? The thorns signify sinners. Then the bush meant the people of the Jews, full of thorns, full of sins. And although the great majesty of God appeared there in the people, the sins did not disappear, just as the thorns were not burned with this fire. If the fire had consumed the thorns, it would mean that the word of the Lord, addressed to the Jews, would have consumed their sins, and that law would have put an end to their iniquities. For the fire in the bush is like the law among the Jews; and the thorns illic tibi expositum est quemadmodum apparuerit Deus per creaturam, angelum. Sic quid miraris quia dicitur, cum apparet angelus, Dixit Deus; et vocavit Deus Moysen, et accessit ad locum; et dixit Dominus ad Moysen? Quia non attenditur templum angelus, sed inhabitator angelí. Ipse enim angelus templum Dei erat. Si enim digntur in nomine habitare et loqui, ut quando propheta loquitur, dicatur, Dixit Deus; How much magis per angelum? Et cum dicitur, Dixit Deus per Isaiam, quid erat Isaiah? Nonne homo portans carnem, natus de patre et matre, sicuti omnes nos? Et tamen loquitur, et quid dicimus in eloquiis ipsius? Haec dicit Dominus (Is 50,1). Quomodo ergo Deus, si Isaiah, nisi quia Deus per Isaiam? Sic et hic loquente angelo dicitur Deus loqui. Quare, nisi quia per angelum Deus? CAPUT I I I. — 3.

Dei apparitio quare in rubo {acta.—Advertite itaque soluta quaestione etiam istud, in cuius rei signum videtur factum, quod in rubo apparuit: et rubus non comburebatur, non incendebatur: et apparebat tanquam ignis, et non incendebat rubum. Putamus rubum bonum aliquid significare, cum sint spinae? Si enim consumpsisset ignis spinas, significaret quia et verbum Domini quod dictum est Iudaeis. consumpsisset peccata iüorum, et Lex illa fi[61]niret iniquitates ipsorum. Si enim sic ignis in rubo, quomodo Lex in Iudaeis; sic sunt spinae rubi,
Moses' calling

They are to the bush as the sins are to the Jews; That is why this fire did not burn the thorns, just as that law did not consume the sins. 4. God speaks to Moses. You already know this and we should not delay, due to the pressure of time. He says, then: I am who I am; He sent me the one he is. When he asked for the name of God, he was answered: I am who I am. You will say to the children of Israel. He who is sent me to you. What does that mean? Oh God, oh our Lord, what is your name? Answer: my name is “Es”. And what does “My name is Es” mean? 3 That I remain eternally, that I cannot change. Because the things that change do not exist, because they do not remain. What does it mean to remain? What is changing was something and will be something; but it is not, since it is mutable. Then the immutability of God deigned to present himself with this word: I am who I am. 5. Why then later did he give himself another name when saying: And the Lord said to Moses: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob; is this my name forever? In the same way that there he called me "he who I am", so now I call myself: I am the God of Abraham, God of Isaac and God of Jacob. Because as God is immutable, he made all things out of mercy, and the Son of God himself deigned to take on changeable flesh, remaining in his being the Word of God, to come and help man. He deigned, therefore, to clothe himself with

mortal flesh that is so that it can be said: I am God of Abraham, God of Isaac and God of Jacob. 6. Now pay attention to the signs that God offered to Moses, Moses saying: If the people tell me that God has not sent you, by what signs will I prove that you sent me? God said to him: Throw away the rod that you are carrying in your hand. He threw the rod, and it became a serpent, and Moses was terrified. The Lord said again: take his tail. And it became a rod, as before. He gave her another sign: Put your hand into your breast. And he put his hand in. Take her out, she took her out and she was white as snow, that is, leprous. Because white color on human skin is a disease. Put it back in the breast. He put it in and regained his color. He gave him a third sign: Take water from the river and throw it on a flat place. He took it, poured it out, and it turned into blood. With these signs the people will listen to you. If he doesn't listen to you the first time, he will listen to you the second or third time. 7. Let us try to explain what all this means, as the Lord helps us. The rod means the kingdom, and the serpent, mortality. In fact, death came to man through the serpent. The Lord deigned to assume that death. That is why the rod, when it reached the earth, took the form of a serpent, because the kingdom of God, which is Christ Jesus, came to earth. He put on mortality and fixed it on the cross. Your Holiness knows well that when in the desert the stubborn and arrogant people murmured against God, they began to suffer the bite of snakes and die from that bite. For his mercy

quomodo peccata Iudaeorum: sic ignis hic non cremavit spinas, quomodo Lex non cremavit peccata. 4. Nomen Dei.—Loquitur autem Dominus ad Moysen (iam illa nostis, et non diutius vos tenere debenmus, propter anxieties temporis): Ego sum qui sum: Misit me qui est. Cum enim quaereret nomen Dei, hoc dictum est: Ego sum qui sum. Haec says filiis Israel: Qui est, misit me ad vos. Quid est hoc? or Deus, or Domine noster, quid vocaris? Est vocor, he said, Quid est, Est vocor? Quia maneo in aeternum, quia mutari non possum. Ea enim quae mutantur, non sunt, quia non petmanent. Quod enim est, manet. Quod autem mutatur, Fuit aliquid, et aliquid erit: non tamen est, quia mutabile est. Ergo incommutabilitas Dei this vocabulo se dignata est intimare, Ego sum qui sum. CAPUT IV.—5. Aliud nomen Dei.—Quid est ergo, quod postea iterum aliud nomen sibi dixit, cum diceretur: Et dixit Deus ad. Moysen: Ego sum Deus Abraham, et Deus Isaac, et Deus lacob; hoc mihi nomen est in sempiternum? Quomodo illac vocor hoc, quia sum; et ecce hac aliud nomen, Ego sum Deus Abraham, et Deus Isaac, et Deus lacob? Quia quomodo est Deus incommutabilis, fecit omnia per misericordiam, et dignitus est ipse Filius Dei mutabilem carnem suscipiendo, manens id quod Verbum Dei est, vinore et subvenire homini. Induit ergo se carne mortali Ule qui est, ut dici posset, Ego sum Deus Abraham, et Deus Isaac, et Deus lacob (Ex 3,15).
See supplementary note 19: The immutability of God, p.750.

6. Signa data Moysi.—Deinde signa iam attendite, quae signa dedit Moysi, cum diceret, Si mihi dixerit populus, Non te misit Deus: quibus signis ostendam quia misisli me? Dictum est, Proice virgam, quam habes in tnanu tua: proiecitque virgam, et factus est serpens, et exhorruit Moyses. Ait iterum Dominus, Apprehende caudam eius, apprehendit, et jacta est virga sicut erat. Dedit et aliud signum: Mitte manum in sinum: et misit eam. Produc eam: produxit, et jacta est alba sicut nix, id est, leprosa. Color enim albus in cute humano vitiosus est. Mitte illam in sinum iterum: misit, et recepit colorem suum. Dedit ei tertíum signum: Tolle aquam de flumine, et funde in aequalem locum: tulit et fudit, et conversa est in sanguinem. In bis signis audiet te populus: si in primo non exaudierit, in secundo autem et in tertio audiet (ib., 4,1-9). CAPUT V.—7. Quid significet virga: quid serpens.—Nos ea quae significant, quantum Deus adiuvat, tendamus edicere. Virga regnum significat; serpens, mortalitatem. A serpente enim homini mors propinata est. Ipsam mortem Dominus dignitus est assumere. Virga ergo veniens in terram, serpentis speciem habuit; quia regnum Dei, quod est Christus Iesus, come ad terram. Mortalitate indutus est, quam infixit in intersection. Novit autem Sanctitas vestra quia quando populus ille in eremo cervicatus et superbus murmurasset adversus Deum, coepit morderi a serpentibus, et ipsis morsibus cadere. Misericordia sua dedit Deus [62] remedium,

God offered the remedy, which remedy provided present health and announced future wisdom. God said to Moses: Hang a bronze serpent from a pole in the middle of the desert and say to the people: Whoever has been wounded, look at this serpent. The wounded men looked at the snake and were healed. The Lord bore witness to this sign in the Gospel, for speaking with Nicodemus he said: As Moses raised up a serpent in the desert, so it is fitting that the Son of Man be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him will not perish but have eternal life, that is, everyone who has been bitten by the serpents of sins may look to Christ, and will have health with the remission of sins. This, then, brothers, is the mortality that the Lord took, and that the Church, his body, whose head is a man in heaven, must have. Thus the Church has the mortality that was inflicted upon her by the persuasion of the serpent. Because we owe death to the sin of the first man, but then we will reach eternal life through Jesus Christ, our Lord. But when do you come to life and return to the kingdom? At the end of the century. That is why Moses took the tail, which is the end, to recover the original figure. 8. What does the hand mean? Without a doubt, the hand means the same people, and the breast means men. What does the bosom of Moses mean? The secret of God. When man lived in the secret of God, he lived unscathed and had good color. He came out of the quod remedium praesentem quidem sanitatem afferebat, sedfuturam sapientiam praedicabat. Ait Moysi: Suspende serpentem aeneum in media eremo in ligno, et dic populo, Quicumque fuerit percussus, serpentem istum intueatur. Et percussi bomines intuebantur serpentem, et sanabantur (Num 21,8.9). Et attestatur Dominus in Gospel tali sign. Nam cum Nicodemo loqueretur, ait: Sicut Moyses exaliavit serpentem in deserto, ka exaltari oportet Yilium hominis; ut omnis qui credit in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam (lo 3,14 et 15). Sed hoc est, quicumque percussus fuerit a serpentibus peccatorum, Christum intueatur, et habebit sanitatem in remissionem peccatorum. CAPUT VI.—Ergo, frattes, ipsa est mortalitas, quae suscepta est a Domino, quam necesse est habere cotpus eius, cuius est caput homo in cáelo. Ita Ecclesia mortalitatem habet, quod vulnus inflictum est per suasionem serpentis. Debemus enim mortem peccato Dtimi hominis: sed per eam ad vitam perveniemus aeternam, per Icsum Christum Dominum nostrum.

Sed quando venit ad vitam, et redit ad regnum? In fine saeculi. Nam ideo caudam tenuit, ubi finis est, ut ad pristinum revocaret. 8. Quid manus et sinus Moysi: quid aqua.—Quid illa manus? Certum est quia et illa manus populum ipsum significat. Sinus hominis what is it? Sinus Moysi secretum Dei. Cum esset homo in secreto Dei, incolumis erat, et bond colore. Exiit a secret Dei, progressus est Adam de
Moses' calling

secret of God, Adam was thrown out of paradise after offending God, and fell ill. That hand turned white; but he returned her to her bosom, by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and she regained her color. And what does water mean? That water means wisdom. Water is often cited as the likeness of wisdom, and so it was said: a fountain of water will be formed in him that springs up to eternal life. But the fact that this water of wisdom turns into blood when it reaches the earth, does it not show us the Word who became flesh and dwelt among us? Definitely. All these things are, then, signs for the future people and mysteries that concern our Lord Jesus Christ. And if there are other sacraments in the ancient books, whether we discover them or not, they ask for an investigator, not a slanderer 4. Let us ask, then, let us search, let us knock, so that they may open to us. Future sacraments were preached to the ancients; We see them already present in the Church. paradiso, offenso Deo, et factus est vitiosus. Facta est ergo manus illa alba: sed rediit ad sinum, per sinum Domini nostri Iesu Christi, et recepit colorem. Quid autem illa aqua? Aqua illa significat sapientiam. Saepe enim posita est aqua in similarityinem sapientiae: et dictum est, Fiet in eo fons aquae salientis in vitam aeternam (lo 4,14). Sed aqua illa sapientia, quae in terra sanguis effecta est, non nobis otendit Verbum carnem factum et habitantem in nobis? Utique ostendit. Omnia ergo futuri populi, signa sunt et mysteria de Domino nostro Iesu Christo. Et si qua allia sunt in veteribus Libris sacramenta, sive illa intellegamus; sive non intellegamus, quaerentem desiderant, non reprehendentem. Petamus ergo, quaeramus et pulsemus, ut aperiatur nobis. lilisfutura praedicta sunt sacramenta: nos praesentia videmus in Ecclesia. Understanding the hidden meaning of Scripture is not only the fruit of man's ability, but above all of the grace of God. God reveals it to whomever he pleases. As in so many other aspects, to receive the gift of God an attitude of humility and subordination is necessary, which, in the specific case, is identified with an attitude of search: this is diametrically opposed to that of the Manichaeans, who from the outset presented themselves as accusing. Augustine comes to tell them: you will never understand the meaning that is hidden in such a mysterious sign. It is necessary, therefore, to pray, to beg, to call.

Theme: The burning bush (Ex 3,21-24). Date: Variety of opinions. All before 412. Place: Carthage. 1. When the divine reading was given about that strange miracle that caught the attention of the servant of God Moses, we also wondered with our hearts, and our interest was intrigued, when we saw that the fire appeared in the bush, and the bush did not burn. Later we noticed that the Holy Scripture had previously said that the angel of the Lord appeared to Moses in the bush, while Moses no longer speaks as with an angel, but as with God. Thirdly we notice that, when Moses asked for the name of God, in order to be able to answer the Israelites who asked what was the name of the God who sent him to them, he answered: I am who I am. And he does not say it just once, but, insisting on repetition, he adds: this you will say to the children of Israel: He who is sent me to you. Finally, after enunciating his name, he further adds: You will say to them: The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, sent me to you.
DE LECTIONE EXODI, DE RUBO IN QUO FLAMMA ERAT ET RUBUS NON COMBUREBATUR

1. Quae warning de apparitione in rubo.—[63] Cum divina lectio legeretur, magnum miraculum, quod Moysen famulum Dei intentissimum fecerat, etiam nos corde exspectavímus; quia intenti etiam ipsi facti sumus, quomodo in rubo apparebat ignis, et rubus non cremabatur. Deinde advertimus sacram Scripturam prius dixisse, quod angelus Domini apparuerit Moysi in rubo (Act 7, 30). Deinde Moyses non iam quasi cum angelo, sed tanquam cum Domino locobatur. Tertio advertimus, quod cum Moyses nomen Dei quaereret, ut haberet quid diceret filiis Israel, interrogantibus quod nomen Dei esset, qui illum ad eos misisset, respond to: Ego sum qui sum. Ñeque hoc transeunter, sed repetitione commendans adiecit: You say itaque filiis Israel: Qui est, misit me ad vos. Postremo iam enuntiato nomine suo, adhuc adiunxit: Haec dices eis: Dominus Deus patrum vestrorum, Deus Abraham, et Deus Isaac, et Deus Iacob misit me ad vos. Et hoc mihi nomen est in aeternum (Ex 3). Of his,

others. This is my name forever. Listen now to what the Lord suggests to me. Great are the divine mysteries, like burdens; If we tried to explain them consistently and sufficiently, our strength and time would not be enough. 2. But what we can say briefly will not be useless, nor vain, nor without some meaning of a symbol. The flame lit in the bush, and the bush did not burn. The bush is a certain kind of thorns, and can mean nothing good, since the earth produced it for the sinner. In fact, when man sinned at the beginning, he was told: The earth will produce thorns and thistles for you. The bush was not burning, that is, it was not caught by the flame, but we should not think that it means anything good either. The flame, in which the angel or the Lord appeared, means something good, and that is why, when the Holy Spirit came, separate tongues appeared, as if of fire; but then we must understand that the bush did not burn, not because of the ineffectiveness of the fire, but because of the hardness of the bush. The bush, which did not burn, means the people who resisted God. The bush therefore means the thorny people of the Jews, to whom Moses was sent. The bush was not burned because the hardness of the Jews, as I said, resisted the law of God. For if that thorny town had not come into meaning, Christ would not have been crowned with thorns by it. 3. That the being who spoke with Moses calls himself an angel of the Lord and Lord, is a great problem and demands not a reckless quod Dominus donat, audite. Magna quidem sunt, tanquam implicates mysteriorum Dei: quae si congruenter et sufficienter conemur evolvere, nec vires, nec tempus sufficient. 2. Rubus flamma inhaerente non crematus quid significat.—Quod ergo breviter possumus dicere, non frustra, non inaniter, non sine alicuius significatione secreti, in rubo flamma erat, et rubus non cremabatur. Rubus enim spinarum est quoddam genus: nec in laude aliqua poni potuit, quod peccatori terra produxit. Nam primitus peccanti homini dictum est, Terra spinas et tribuios pariet tibi (Gen 3:18). affirmer, but a cautious investigator. There are two sentences here that we can present: both are in accordance with the Catholic faith, whichever is authentic. By saying whatever is authentic, I mean what the person who wrote it intended to give. When in studying the Scriptures we affirm something that the writer perhaps did not affirm, we should not affirm something that contradicts the rule of faith, the rule of truth, or the rule of piety. Therefore I propose the two sentences. And maybe there is a third that I don't know. Of the two that I propose, choose the one you like. Some say that he is called the angel of the Lord and Lord because he was Christ, of whom the prophet clearly says that he is an angel of the great counsel. Because angel is a name of function, not of nature 2. An angel in Greek is called the one who in Latin we call messenger. Messenger is a word of action: acting, that is, announcing, he is called nuncio. And who denies that Christ announced the kingdom of heaven to us? Furthermore, the angel, that is, the nuncio, is sent by someone who announces something through him. And who doubts that Christ was sent, who says so many times: I did not come to do my will, but the will of him who sent me? That is why it is properly sent. Thus, the pool of Siloam was translated Sent. That's why he sent the blind man there, whom he put mud in his eyes, to wash his face. Only Dominus dicitur, magna quaestio est, nec temerarium debent habere affirtnatorem, sed cautum inquisitorem. Duae sunt autem sententiae, quae hinc proferri possunt, quarum quaelibet vera sit, ambae secundum fidem sunt. Quod dixi, quaenam earum vera sit; hoc dixi, quidnam eotum sensetit qui scripsit. Ergo both sententias I propose: sit fortassis et tertia, quae me latet. Ex his autem duabus propositis, eligatis quam volueritis. Aliqui dicunt ideo et angelum Domini dictum et Dominum, quia Christus erat, de quo aperte propheta dicit quod sit magni consilii Angelus (Is 9:6). Angelus enim officii nomen est, non naturae. Nam angelus graece, qui latine nuntius appellatur. Nuntius ergo actionis nomen est: agendo, id est, aliquid nuntiando, nuntius appellatur. Quis neget Christum nuntiasse nobis regnum caelorum? Deinde angelus, id est nuntius, mittitur ab eo qui per eum aliquid nuntiat.

Et quis neget Christum missum? qui toties dicit, Non veni faceré voluntatem meam, sed voluntatem eius qui me misit (lo 6,38); ipse proprie missus. Nam Siloe, pool island, Missus interpreter. Ideo cui oculos luto inunxit,

Because there is no shortage of heretics who affirm 3 that the nature of the Father and the Son are different and distant, and that they are not of one and the same substance. On the other hand, the Catholic faith believes that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are one God, a trinity of the same substance, inseparable and equal, not confused by mixture or separated by division. Therefore, those who try to persuade that the Son is not of the same substance as the Father, argue that the Son was seen by the fathers. The Father, they say, was not seen; The invisible and the visible are of different nature. Therefore, it was said of the Father: whom no one saw nor could see. Then he whom they saw, not only Moses, but also Abraham; and not only Abraham, but also Adam himself, and the other fathers, we must believe or understand that it was not God the Father, but the Son, the creature. Catholics don't say that. What do they say? God the Father, God the Son: the Father unalterable, the Son unalterable; eternal the Father, coeternal the Son; invisible the Father, invisible the Son. If you call the Father invisible and the Son visible, you distinguished, or rather, separated the substances. How did you find grace when you lost faith? The problem is resolved, then, like this: God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are their own and invisible nature. He appeared when inde lavare faciem iussit (ib., 9,7). Nullius enim visus aperitur, nisi eius qui a Christo mundatur. Ergo idem angelus, idem Dominus. 4. In ea opinione cavendum Arianorum argumentum.—Sed hic occurrit aliquid praecavendum. Catholica non hoc dicit. Sed quid dicit? Deus Pater, Deus Filius; incommutabilis Pater, incommutabilis Filius; aeternus Pater, coaeternus Filius; invisibilis Pater, invisibilis Filius. Nam si dixeris Patrem invisibilem, Filium visibilem; distinxisti, immo vero separasti substañtias. Quomodo gratiam invenisti, qui fidem perdidisti? Those who think that he was actually an angel of the Lord, not Christ, but an angel sent, must give us the reason why he is called Lord. And they respond: «As in the Scriptures a prophet speaks and it is said that the Lord speaks, not because the Lord is a prophet, but invisibilis est: apparuit autem quando voluit, cui voluit; non ut est, sed ut voluit cui serviunt omnia. Si enim anima tua cum sit invisibilis in corpore tuo, ut appareat profert vocem, et vox in qua apparet anima tua cum loqueris, non est substantia animae tuae; aliud est illa, aliud est vox; et tamen apparet, et in ea re quae ipsa non est: sic et Deus si in igne apparuit, non est ignis; si in fumo apparuit, non est fumus; si in sonó apparuit, non est sonus. Respondent et ipsi: Sicut in Scripturis propheta loquitur, et dicitur quia Dominus Unquestionably, the theological content of Saint Augustine's sermons is very high. No topic is left unexplored in his preaching, and always with sufficient clarity to be understood by those simple people who listened to him with enthusiasm. And how was it administered? Promulgated, he says, through the angels and through a mediator. 7. So the angel, and in the angel the Lord, said to Moses, when he asked him his name: I am who I am. This you will say to the children of Israel. He who is sent me to you. Being is a word of immutability. Everything that changes stops being what it was and begins to be what it was not. The being is. Only one who does not change has a true being, a pure being, an authentic being. He is the true being, of whom it is said: you change everything and it will change, but you are always the same. What does it mean: I am who I am, if not I am eternal? I am not a creature, nor heaven, nor earth, nor angel, nor virtue, nor throne, nor domination, nor power. Since this name is proper to eternity, the dignity with which it takes the name of mercy is greater6. I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. That name was for him, this one for us. If he had wanted to be only himself, what would we be? If he understood, or rather, since Moses understood, when they said to him: I am who I am, he who is sent me to you, he believed that this sublimity was excessive for men, and he saw that this sublimity was far from men. Topic: The ten plagues of Egypt and the ten commandments of God. Date: Around 411. Place: Carthage. 1. To God our Lord, whose servants we are, praise is dedicated in a certain place of Scripture: You arranged everything with measure, number and weight. Furthermore, apostolic doctrine teaches us to understand and contemplate the invisible things of God through the things he made, and to investigate those that latent by the manifest things. Therefore, creation, questioned in a certain way everywhere, with its very beauty, as with a voice, answers that it has the Lord God as its creator. Finally, the Apostle remembers that everything that was written in the books called the Old Testament happened in figure: it was written for our warning, for those who are coming to the end of the ages. When we diligently study and discuss, and prudently follow and discover those things that in their nature originate apparently fortuitously, we see that they commend the praise of the Creator and that divine providence, which spreads itself everywhere, and disposes, as has been said, smoothly all things, reaching strongly from one end to another end. Well, how much better will that happen in those things that are given to us?
DECEM PLAGIS ET DECEM PRAECEPTIS

1. Domino Deo nostro, cuius cultores sumus, in laude dictum est quodam scribturarum loco: Omnia in mensura et numero et poniere disposuisti (Wis 11,21). Unde interrogata quodammodo ubique creature, Dominum Deum se artificem habere, ipsa speciei suae quadam quasi voce responder. Deinde apostolus ea, quae conscribta sunt in libris, quod dicitur testamentum vetus in figura contigisse commemorat; scribta autem sunt ad correptionem nostram, in quos finis saeculorum obvenit (1 Cor 10:11). Proinde, carissimi, si ea, quae videntur in rerum natura quasi fortuito provenire, perscrutata diligenter atque discussa, et prudenter vestigata et inventa laudem intimate creatoris, divinamque providentiam per cuneta diffusam, et disposentem, ut dictum est, suaviter •omnia, cum attingit a fine usque in finem fortiter (cf. narrate, not only events, but also recommended in the divine letters? The brothers have presented us with a problem, or rather, an investigation and discussion, about the meaning of the ten plagues that the Egyptians suffered and about the ten commandments with which the people of God are instructed. That is why we will try to explain it to you in the name of our Lord, with his grace and help, as you strive with me to pay attention to your hearts. Those who raised the issue know they raised it; and remember that we do not bring it here recklessly. Those of you who did not raise it, also listen to what we can say, so that the brothers' proposal is everyone's concern and the presentation of my ministry serves as food for the community. I hope that God will help, if not for me, certainly for you, to say what I should say and what is useful to hear; In this way, walking together on the path of truth, hastening together to reach the homeland and recognizing the will of God's law, we will deserve to be free from the enemies and robbers of our pilgrimage. 2. There are ten plagues with which Pharaoh's people were punished. And ten are the precepts with which the people of God were instructed. Let's look at it, brothers, since bodily facts must be spiritually understood. We do not believe that these are only sayings and writings, but not facts; but rather we accept the facts as we read that they occurred. Sin embargomagis ea, quae non solum facta, verum etiam divinis litteris commendata tecitantur? Unde propositara nobis a fratribus quaestionem, immo inquisitionem et disputationem, quid sibi velit, quod decem plagis percutiuntur Aegyptii, et decem praeceptis instruitur populus Dei, suscepimus in nomine Domini Dei nostri, adarvante ipso et donor, adnitente nobiscum pia intentione cordis vestri, quantum possumus, I will explain. Qui proposuerunt, quod proposuerunt sciunt, id est, proposuisse se noverunt, nec me hoc tempore ad vos protulisse rememberantur. Quicumque autem non proposuistis, pariter audite quod possumus; ut propositum fratrum cura sit omnium, et expositum ministerii nostri alimentum sit Universorum. Arbitramur enim ipsum adiuturum, etsi non propter nos, certe propter vos, ut ea dicamus, quae et dici oportet, et audire utile est; ut in via veritatiseius pariter ambulantes, et ad patriam pariter festinantes, hostes et insidiatores itineris nostri, agnoscendo voluntatem legis Dei, Evitare mereamur. 2.

Decem sunt plaguee, quibus populus Pharaonis percussus est: decem sunt praecepta, quibus Dei populus instructus est. Videamus ergo, [171] fratres, quoniam corporaliter facta spirítualiter sunt intellegenda: non enim negamus esse facta, ut putemus tantum dicta atque conscripta, non facta; sed facta credimus, quemadmodum facta legimus, et tamen From questions like these, according to the saint's confession, some Augustinian works were born: Exposition of some propositions on the epistle to the Romans (Retractiones I 23,1); 83 various questions (ibid., I 26), etc.
The ten plagues and the ten commandments

So, according to apostolic doctrine, we know that those events were shadows of future things. We think, therefore, that we must understand the events spiritually, but we cannot deny the facts. So let no one say: "It is written that water turned to blood in the plague of the Egyptians, but that means something, since it could not really be verified." Whoever speaks like this seeks the will of God in such a way that he already insults the power of God. How not? If recording could mean, couldn't it mean realizing? Weren't Isaac and Ishmael born? They were born, they were men, they came from Abraham, one from the slave woman, the other from the free woman. And although they were men, and had been born, they represented two Testaments, the Old and the New. Placing, then, the events that occurred firmly on their foundation, we must seek their significance; lest, if we remove the foundation, we seem to want to build in the air 2. And I think, therefore, that all those who disdain the ten commandments of the law and do not observe them, suffer spiritually what the Egyptians suffered bodily. I advance this while I explain it with the help of the Lord, and for that I want you to be attentive and pray for me, so that I may tell you something useful for you. As for me, perhaps I think so; but when I speak, I serve you. 3. Be careful above all not to deceive yourselves about the number: the first occurrence does not belong to these ten plagues, although it is right in sign: the rod converted into seripsa facta umbras Fuisse Futurerum apostolica doctrina cognoscimus. Putamus ergo spiritaliter esse investigada, quae facta sunt, facta tamen esse deniale non possumus. Nemo ergo dicat: Scribtum est quidem, aquam conversam in sanguinem in plague Aegyptiorum; sed significat aliquid, non enim revera fieri potuit. Hoc qui dicit, ita quaerit voluntatem Dei, ut iniuriam faciat potentiae Dei. Quid enim? If saying means potuit, etiam doing non potuit? An numquid non est natus Isaac, aut non Ismahel? Nati werent, nomines weret; et ex Abraham nati erant et unus ex ancilla, alter de libera. Quamvis ergo nomines Fuissent, quamvis nati essent, figurarunt tamen duo testamenta, vetus et novum. Ita prius in fundament posita rerum gestarum firmitate significantiam debenmus inquirere, ne subtracto fundament in aere velle aedificare video.

Arbitror ergo omnes, qui decem legis praecepta contempnunt, et non observant, spiritaliter pati ea, quae Aegyptii corporaliter passi sunt; hoc propositum doñee in adiutorio domini explicem, attempts vos voló et orantes pro nobis, ut dicamus utilia vobis. Quod enim ad nos pertinet, fortasse cogitamus; quod autem loquimur, vobis servimus. 3. Illud ergo prius accipite, ne in numero fallamini: ad pestas istas decem non pertinere, quod primo factum est signi causa, ut virga in serpentem converteretur. Aditus enim erat ipse ad Pharaonem, quo com* Yéage supplementary note 5: Historicity of biblical facts, p,744.

think. It was about the audience before Pharaoh, to propose that Moses would lead the people out of Egypt. Those who were stubborn were not yet punished, but were frightened with a divine sign. It is not necessary here, nor have I proposed it, to talk about the rod turned into a snake. But since I have mentioned it out of necessity, to avoid error in the number, and there should not remain in the mind of any listener scruple of not having understood, I will briefly say that the rod means the kingdom of God, and that that kingdom is the people of God; The serpent means the time of this mortality, since death was caused by the serpent; as if, when men fell from the hand of the Lord to the earth, they had become mortal; Therefore, when Moses threw the staff out of his hand, it became a serpent. Pharaoh's magicians performed a similar wonder: when they threw their staffs they turned into snakes. But the serpent, that is, the rod of Moses, devoured all the serpents of the wise men. And finally, when he took it by the tail, it became a rod again, and the kingdom returned to his hand. The rods of the magicians are the people of the wicked. When those people, defeated in the name of Christ, are transferred to his Body, it is as if they were devoured by the rod of Moses, until we return the kingdom of God to the hand of God, at the end of the mortal age, symbolized in the tail of the serpent. Great sign: be it, be it. You heard what you should think; Hear now what you should avoid. 4. The first commandment of the law is to worship one God. You will have, he says, no other gods besides me. And the primemendabatur Moyses educturus ex Aegypto populum Dei; nondum autem contumaces feriebantur, thirst divine sign iam terrebantur. Ñeque nunc opus est, ñeque ptopositum est, de ipsa virga in serpentem [172] conversa aliquid dicere. Verumtamen, quia eius mentionem necessitate fecimus, ne quisquam in numero erraret, nec debent in cuiusquam auditoris animo tamquam non intellectae rei scrupulus remanere, breviter dicimus, virgam significare regnum Dei, idemque regnum esse utique populum Dei; serpentem autem, tempus mortalitatis huius: mors enim a serpente propinata est. Tamquam ergo cadentes de manu domini in terram mortales effecti sunt; unde proiecta virga ex manu Moysi serpens effecta est. Fecerunt et magi Pharaonis similiter: virgis eorum proiectis serpentes facti sunt.

Sed prius serpens Moysi, id est, virga Moysi devoravit omnes serpentes magorum; tune demum cauda conpraehensa identidem virga facta est, et regnum remeavit ad manum. Sunt enim virgae magorum populi impiorum: qui tamen populi impiorum, victi Christi nomine, cum in eius corpus transferuntur, tamquam a serpente Moysi devorantur, doñee redeat regnum Dei ad manum Dei, sed in fine mortalis saeculi, quod significat cauda serpentis. Magnum signum: fiat, fiat. Audistis quid debenatis desiderare: audite quid debenatis vitare. 4. Primum praeceptum in lege de colendo uno Deo: non erunt tibi, inquit, dii alii praeter me (Ex 20,3). you have ten plagues and the ten commandments

The plague of the Egyptians is water turned into blood. Compare the first commandment with the first plague. Compare God, from whom everything comes, with water, from which everything is generated. And what does blood mean, if not mortal flesh? What then is the conversion of water into blood, except that his heart was darkened? Saying they were wise, they became fools; and they converted the incorruptible glory of God into the likeness of an image of corruptible man, birds, four-footed animals, and serpents. The glory of an incorrupt God is like water; The likeness of the image of corruptible man, birds, quadrupeds and serpents is like blood. This is done in the hearts of the wicked, since God remains immutable 3; Although the Apostle says they converted, God does not change. 5. Second precept: You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain; For whoever takes the name of the Lord his God in vain will not be clean. The name of the Lord our God, Jesus Christ, is the Truth, for he himself said: I am the truth. And as the truth cleanses, vanity defiles. He who speaks truth, speaks of God's things, because he who speaks lies, speaks of his own; Therefore, speaking truth is speaking rationally; and he who speaks vanity, gurgles rather than speaks. That's right, since the second commandment is love of truth, to which love of vanity is contrary. The truth speaks, vanity bubbles. See now, secondly, the second plague, contrary to this commandment. What is that second plague? He converses her in sanguinem. Conpara primum praeceptum primae pestae. Deum unum, ex quo sunt omnia, in similarity intellege aquae, ex qua generatur omnia. Quo autem pertinet sanguis, nisi ad carnem mortalem? Quid est ergo conversio aquae in sanguinem, nisi quia obscuratum est insipiens cor eorum? Dicentes enim se esse sapientes, stulti facti sunt; et commutaverunt gloriam incorruptibilis Dei in similitu\X¡y\dinem imaginis corruptibilis hominis (Rom 1,21.22.23). Gloria incorruptibilis Dei, sicut aqua; similarity imaginis corruptibilis hominis, sicut sanguis. Et hoc quidem fit in corde impiorum, nam Deus incommutabilis manet: ñeque enim quia et apostolus dixit commutaverunt, ideo mutatus est Deus. 5. Secundum praeceptum: Non accipies nomen Domini Dei tui in vanum; qui enim accipit nomen Domini Dei sui in vanum, non mundabitur (Ex 20,7). Nomen Domini Dei nostri Iesu Christi veritas est: ipse enim dixit, ego sum veritas (lo 14,6). Veritas ergo mundat, vanitas inquinat.

Et quoniam, qui loquitur veritatem, from Dei loquitur —qui enim loquitur mendacium, from suo loquitur (lo 8,44)— veritatem loqui est rationabiliter loqui; vanitatem autem loqui est strepere potius quam loqui. Merit, quia secundum praeceptum est dilectio veritatis, cui contra est dilectio vanitatis; loquitur autem veritas, perstrepit vanitas:

abundance of frogs. There you have vanity meant in a congruent way, if you notice the loquacity of the frogs 4. See how the lovers of the truth do not take the name of the Lord their God in vain and speak wisdom among the perfect and even among the imperfect; It is not that they speak what they cannot understand; but they do not depart from the truth nor give themselves over to vanity. Perhaps the imperfect ones will not understand when something about the Word of God is explained more fully, speaking to God before God, who made all things, and, on the other hand, they can understand what Paul speaks among men, as among infants in Christ Jesus, to Christ Jesus, and him crucified. That does not mean that this will be true and this will be vanity. It would be vanity if we said that Christ did not suffer, but that he feigned death, that his wounds were fantastic, that he had not shed real blood from the wounds, but simulated one; who had shown false scars as a result of false injuries. But when we say that all these things were true, we put certain, express facts, which we believe verified and we preach them; Although we do not speak according to divine sublimity and according to immutable truth, we do not slide into vanity either. Those who affirm that all these things were false and simulated in Christ 5 are frogs crying in a muddy puddle. They can produce the roar of the voice, they cannot insinuate a doctrine of wisdom. Those who speak in the Church huic praecepto secundocontram videte secundara plaguem. What is the second plague? Ranarum abundantia. Habes expressam significatam vanitatem, si attendas ranarum loquacitatem. Vide amatores vetitatis, non accipiientes in vanum nomen domini Dei sui, loqui sapientiam Inter perfections (cf. 1 Cor 2:6), etiam inter inperfectos: non quidem loqui quod capere non possunt, non tamen recedere a veritate, et pergere in vanitatem. Quamvis enim inperfecti non capiant, si quid paulo excelsius fuerit disputatum de Verbo Dei, Deo apud Deum, per quod facta sunt omnia; possintque capere, quod Inter eos loquitur Paulus tamquam inter pvulos, Chris[174]tum lesum, et hunc crucifixum (1 Cor 2,2), non tamen illa est veritas, et ista vanitas. Vanitas autem esset, si Christum mortem non ímplevisse, sed finxisse diceremus: si vulnera illa in phantasmate Fuisse, si sanguinem non verum sed simulatum de vulneribus emanasse, si false eum scars tamquam post false vulnera demonstrasse.

Cum vero ista omnia vera dicimus, facta dicimus, certa, expressa, impleta credimus et praedicamus; quamvis de sublimi illius et de incommutabili veritate non loquamur, non tamen imus in vanitatem. Qui autem illa omnia in Christo false et simulata dicunt, ranae sunt clamantes in palude: strepitum voris habere possunt, doctrinam sapientiae insinuare non pos4 In the Enarration to Psalm 11:21, it says: "extremely charlatan vanity is called a frog." united to the truth, they speak truth, by which everything was created; They speak truth, the Word who became flesh and dwelt among us; They speak truth to Christ, born of God, unique of the only, only begotten and co-eternal; They say the truth when they affirm that he received the form of a servant, that he was born of the Virgin Mary, suffered, was crucified, resurrected and ascended; They always tell the truth, either one that a child can understand, or one that the child cannot understand; They speak truth in bread and milk, in the bread of adults and in the milk of infants. Because that same bread, to make milk, is made by meat. Those who contradict that truth and, deceived in their vanity, deceive others, are frogs that provide tedium to the ear, not food to the mind. Listen, finally, to those who speak rationally: they are not messages or words whose voices are not heard, they are not vain voices, because their sound reached all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. And if you want to remember the frogs in the opposite sense, remember that little verse from the psalm: vanities spoke each one to his neighbor. 6. Third commandment: Remember to sanctify the Sabbath day. In this third commandment a certain promulgation of rest, repose of the heart, tranquility of the mind, which a good conscience works, is hinted at. There is sanctification, because there is the spirit of God. See that vacation, that is, that stillness, when saying: On whom does my spirit rest? About the humble, quiet and afraid of my words. The restless are detached from the Holy Spirit, they are lovers of fights, semsunt. Denique in ecclesia loquuntur haerentes veritati veritatem, per quem facta sunt omnia: veritatem, Verbum carnem factum et habitantem in nobis: veritatem, Christum natum de Deo, unum de uno, unigenitum et coaeternum: veritatem, accepta forma servi natum ex Virgine Maria, passum, crucifixum, resurgentem, ascendant; ubique veritatem, et quam parvulus capere potest, et quam parvulus capere non potest: veritatem et in pane et in lacte, in pane magnorum, in lacte parvulorum. idem quippe pañis, ut lac fiat, per carnem traicitur. Qui autem huic veritati contradicunt, et in sua vanitate decepti decipiunt, ranae sunt taedium afferentes auribus, non cibum mentibus. Audi denique homines rationabiliter loquentes: Ñon sunt loquellae ñeque sermones, quorum non audiantur voices eorum; be voices non inane, quia in omnem terram exiit sonus eorum, et in fines orbis terrae verba eorum (Ps 18,4.5).

Si autem et ranas vis e contrari in[175]tellegere, illum versum psalmi recolé: Vana locutus est unusquisque ad proximum suum (Ps 11,3). 6. Tertium praeceptum: Memento diem sabbati sanctificare eum (Ex 20,8). In tertio isto praecepto insinuatur quaedam vacationis indictio, quies cordis, tranquillitas mentís, quam facit bona conscientia: ibi sanctificatio, quia ibi Spiritus Dei. Denique videte vacationem, hoc est, quietem: Super quem, inquit, requiescit spiritus meus? Super humilem, et quietum, et trementem verba mea (Is 6:2). Inquieti ergo resiliunt ab

brats of slander, more fond of discussion than of vanity, and because of their restlessness they reject the rest of the spiritual Sabbath. Against the uneasiness of these such, as to admit into their hearts the Sabbath, or sanctification of the spirit of God, they are told: be meek when you hear the word, that you may understand it. And what am I to understand? To God, who tells you: «leave your restlessness; calm in your heart that certain tumult that causes corruption in you due to the ghosts that fly and afflict you; cut that.” Thus you will understand God who tells you: Rest and see that I am the Lord. Because of your restlessness you do not want to rest and, blinded by the corruption of your discussions, you demand to see what you cannot. Pay attention, then, to this third plague, contrary to the third commandment: the Cinpheths came up from the mire in the land of Egypt. They are certain very small, very restless mosquitoes, which fly disorderly, get into the eyes, and do not allow man to rest; You scare them away and they come back, you throw them away and they come back, just like the vain ghosts in the hearts of discussants. Hold the commandment, avoid the plague.

8. The fifth commandment is: You shall not fornicate7. And the fifth plague is death in the Egyptian flocks. Let's compare. Let's take a fornicating man, not satisfied with his marriage. He does not want to tame within himself the appetite for meat, which is common to us and to animals. Beasts also mate and engender; On the other hand, reasoning and understanding are typical of men. Thus, reason, which presides over the mind, must restrain with its government and dominion the movements of the lower flesh, not let go of the reins immoderately and illicitly, without consideration or order. That is why nature, by institution of the Creator, causes animals to mate only at certain times. At other times, the animal is not inhibited by reason, but is hindered by the cooling of its instinct. Man can always be active, because he can slow down his movements. The Creator gave you the dominion of reason. He offered you precepts of continence, like reins over the lower beasts. And because you have what the animal cannot, you expect what the animal cannot. You work a little to contain yourself, while the animal does not work; but you will always enjoy eternity, which the animal does not enter. If the effort tires you, be encouraged by the reward. Patience itself consists of slowing down the inner movement and not letting go of the reins without considering what you have in common with the beast, as if you were a beast. If in you you despise yourself and disdain the image of God,

7. The fourth commandment is: Honor your father and mother. This commandment is opposed by the fourth plague of the Egyptians: cynomia is a dog fly: it is a Greek word. It is dogs not to recognize parents; There is nothing so canine as that those who engendered are not recognized. No wonder dog puppies are born blind 6. Spiritu sancto, rixarum amatares, calumniatum seminatores, contentionis quam veritatis cupidiores, disturbinge sua non ad se admittunt quietem sabbati spititalis. Contra istorum disturbinginem dicitur, tamquam ut sabbatum habeant in corde sanctificationem Spiritus Dei: Esto mansuetus ad audiendum verbum, ut intellegas (Eccli 5,13). Quid intellecturus sum? Deum dicentem: Cessa ab problemaine tua: non sit tumultus quidam in corde tuo per corruptionem volitantibus phantasmatis et compungentibus te, non sit; ita Deum enim intellecturus is dicentem tibi: Vacate et videte quia ego sum Deus (Ps 45,11). Tu per disturbingem vacare non vis, contentionumque tuarum corruptione caecatus demand videre quod non potes. Attende enim et contram tertiam plaguem huic praecepto tertio: scinifes natae sunt in terra Aegypti de limo. Muscae quaedam sunt minutissimae, inquietissimae, inordinate volitantes, in oculos inruentes, non permittentes hominem quiescere, dum abiguntur et inruunt, dum abactae rursus redeunt, sicut omnino vana phantasmata cordis contentiosorum. Tenete praeceptum, cavete pestum. [176] 7. Quartum praeceptum est: Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam (Ex 20:12). Huic contrara quarta Aegyptiorum pest, cynomyia. What is cynomyia? Est canina musca: graecum vocabulum est. Caninum est, parentes non agnoscere: nihil tam caninum, quam cum illi qui genuerunt non agnoscuntur. Merit ergo et catuli canum caeci nascuntur. See Ennarration to Psalm 77:27.

8. Quintum praeceptum est: Non moechaberis (Ex 20,14); Fifth plague is mors in pécora Aegyptiorum. Comparemus. Da hominem moechantem, coniugio non contentum suo: appetitum quendam carnis in se domare non vult, qui est nobis pecoribusque communis. Etenim concumbere et generare etiam pecorum est; ratiocinari et intellegere hominum est. Ideo ratio, quae praesidet in mente, motus inferioris carnis tamquam regnans et dominans frenere debent, non inmoderate et inlicite passim vageque laxare. Ideoque ipsis pecoribus natura datum est, instituente creatore, ut non moveantur ad feminas et ad concubitum nisi certis temporibus: ñeque enim ratione se cohibet alio tempore pecus, sed omnino ipso motu frigescente torpescit. Homo autem ideo semper moveri potest, quia et frere motum potest. Tibi dominationem rationis creator dedit; tibi praecepta continentiae tamquam in inferior beasts lora concessit: tenes tu quod pecus non potest, et ideo speras tu quod pecus non potest. Laboras aliquantum in continendo, non laborat pecus; sed gaudebis semper in aeternitate, ad quam non pervenit pecus. Si opus fatiguet, merces consoletur: et ipsa enim patientia est, interiorem motum basare, et, quod habes commune cum pecore, non tamquam pecus in omnia relaxare. in which he created you, overcome by the appetite of beasts, you will be a beast, as if man were lost from you; It is not that you acquire the nature of the beast, for you do not listen to him who says: do not be like the horse and the mule, which have no understanding. The sixth plague consisted of pustules on the body, blisters that itched and oozed, and burning ulcers from the ashes of the furnace. This is what homicidal souls are like. They burn with anger, because through the wrath of murder brotherhood perishes. Men burn with anger, but also with grace. The burning of health and that of an ulcer are different, however. Burning blisters on the entire body are intentional homicides. Well, but not health; They boil, but not with the spirit of God. Both those who want to help and those who want to kill feel boiling; that one, of the commandment; this one, of the disease; that one, of good works; this one, of putrid ulcers. If we could see the soul of murderers, we would mourn it more than the putrefied bodies of those with ulcers. 10. Follow the seventh commandment: Thou shalt not steal. The seventh plague follows: hail in the crops. What you steal against the commandment, you lose to heaven. Because no one achieves unjust gain without fair harm. For example, he who steals

acquire a dress; but, according to heavenly judgment, he loses faith. Where there was profit there is harm; visible profit, invisible damage; profit for their blindness, harm for the cloud of the Lord. Nothing happens without providence, darlings. Or do you really think that what men suffer, they suffer because God falls asleep? It seems that things are going out of order, the clouds gather, the rain falls, the hail falls, the thunder shakes the earth and the lightning scares away. It seems that everything is out of order and does not concern divine providence. Against such thoughts guard that psalm that says: Praise the Lord, from the earth (when praise comes from heaven), dragons and all the deeps, fire, hail, snow, frost, spirit of tempest, who keep their word. Therefore, he who through his evil desire steals externally, by the judgment of God receives the hailstorm internally. Oh, if the thief could see the field of his heart! Without a doubt he would cry, not finding what he had put in the mouth of his mind even if in his theft he found what he was greedily slurping down his throat. Greater is the hunger of the inner man, greater is the hunger, more dangerous is the plague and more serious is the death. There are many dead people who walk and many starving people who enjoy their vain riches. Finally, Scripture calls the servant of God rich inwardly, saying: the hidden man of your heart, who before God is rich. He is not rich before men, but before God; It is rich where God sees. What does it profit you if you steal where man does not see, and are stoned where God sees?

Quod si contempseris te in te, et imaginem Dei, in qua fecit te, neglexeris, victus cupiditate bestiarum, tamquam amisso homine eris pecus: non quasi convetsus in naturam pecoris, sed in hominis forma habens similarityinem pecotis, qui non [177] audis dicentem: Nolite esse sicut equus et mulus, non habentes intellectum (Ps 31,9). Sed forte eligís tibi esse pecus, et libera vagari libídine, nulla lege appetitum carnis ad continentiam refrenare? Attende plaguem: si pecus esse non times, saltem morí sicut pecus time. 9. Such sunt animae homicidales: ardent ira, quia per iram homicidii fraternitas deperiit. Ardent nomines iracundia, ardent et gratia: sed alius est fervor sanitatis, alius fervor ulceris. Ardentes papulae per totum corpus concepta homicidia scatent, et sanum non est. Fervet, sed non de Spiritu Dei. Nam et qui vult subvenire fervet, et qui vult occidere fervet: ille praecepto, ille morbo; ille bonis operibus, ille saniosis ulceribus. Si possemus videre animas homicidarum, plus plangeremus quam putrescentia corpora ulceratorum. 10. Sequitur non furaberis (Ex 20:15), praeceptum septimum, et plague septima, grando in fructibus. As a comparison for this plague, nothing else occurs to me (perhaps those who search diligently will find something better) than to see that men keep everything they have for their heirs, and among these nothing is dearer than the firstborn. Desiring your neighbor's property is condemned here. He who snatches by theft covets. Who steals his neighbor's possession, except because he desires it? But about theft we already saw another commandment. There you must also include plunder. The Scripture would not speak of theft and plunder if it did not want you to understand that, if it is a crime to steal secretly, it deserves a greater penalty to take away by violence. Therefore, stealing from those who do not consent, whether secretly or openly, already has its commandment. But it is also not lawful to desire your neighbor's property even if you claim to be a legitimate heir, because God warns you in your heart. Those who claim to possess other people's property with fair appearances try to have the dying make them heirs. Nothing seems as fair as possessing what has been inherited, since it is owned by common law. «What do you have to do with it, good man? "They left it to me, I got the inheritance, I will read the will to you." Nothing seems fairer to avarice than this reply. You praise him who seems to possess justly; God condemns the one who covets unjustly. See who you are when you want another to make you his heir. You do not want him to have other heirs, among which the preferred ones are the firstborn. Therefore, you are punished in your firstborn, because by coveting other people's goods you seek with an appearance of right what was not rightfully owed to you.

You, abandoning your only God, who is like the legitimate husband of the soul, want to commit fornication with many demons; and, what is more serious, you do not act as if you were openly abandoning and repudiating God, as apostates do, but you remain in your husband's house and there you admit adulterers. Those who do not want to maintain chastity while married, and there are many such people, do not want me to say this. But I have to say it, whether they want it or not.
