If you become his adversary when you do not do what he tells you, I will become his adversary if I do not say what he tells me to say. 4. Perhaps I have spent too much time on what I have said? I have assumed that your charity worships one God. I have assumed this because of the Catholic faith that is in you, since you believe that the Son of God is equal to the Father. Do not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, thinking that the Son of God is a creature. Indeed, every creature is subject to vanity. You believe that he is equal to the Father, God of God, Word in God, Word God, by whom everything was created, light of light, coeternal with him who begat him, one with him who begat him. You believe that this Word assumed a creature, taking on the mortality of the Virgin Mary, and that he suffered for us. That is what we read and believe for our salvation. And I have not stopped at that point in exhorting you to do it and do it for future hope.

ut labors; cum ad hoc debenas laborare, ut requiescas. Dicitur tibi, Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam. Tu autem contumeliam irrogas parentibus, quam non vis pati a filiis tuis. Dicitur tibi, Non occides. Tu autem occidere vis inimicum tuum: et ideo forte non facis, quia times iudicem hominem, non quia cogitas Deum. Do you ignore quia ille testis est cogitationum? Illo vivo quem vis morí, te homicidam tenet in corde. Dicitur tibi, Non moechaberis (Ex 20,1-14); id est, non ibis ad aliquam aliam praeter uxorem tuam. Tu autem demandis hoc ab uxore, et non vis hoc reddere uxori: et cum debenas in virtute praecedere uxorem, quoniam castitas virtus est; tu sub uno Impetu libidinis cadis, et vis uxorem tuam victricem esse, tu victus iacens: et cum tu caput sis uxoris tuae, praecedit te ad Deum, cuius caput es. Vis domum tuam capite deorsum penderé? Caput enim mulieris est vir: ubi autem melius vivit mulier quam vir, capite deorsum pendet domus. Si caput est vir, melius debent vivere vir, et praecedere in ómnibus bonis factis uxorem suam; ut illa imitatetur virum, et sequatur caput suum. Quomodo caput Ecclesiae Christus est, et hoc iubetur Ecclesiae ut sequatur caput suum, et ut per vestigia ambulet capitis sui: sic uniuscuiusque domus habet caput virum, et tanquam corpus feminam (Eph 5,23). Quo caput ducit, illuc debent corpus sequi. Quare ergo vult caput iré, quo non vult ut corpus sequatur? Quare vult iré vir, quo non vult ut uxor sequatur? Haec iubendo

sermo Dei adversarius est. Nolunt enim homines faceré quod vult sermo Dei. Et quid dicam, quia adversarius est sermo Dei, quoniam iubet? Timeo ne ego ipse adversarius sim quibusdam, quia haec loquor. Quid ad pertinet me? Fortem me faciat qui terret ut loquar, ut non timeam querelas hominum. Nam qui nolunt castitatem servare uxoribus suis (et abundant tales), [78] nolunt me ista dicere. Sed velint nolint, dicturus sum. Si enim vos non exhortor ut cum adversary concordetis, ego cum illo in lite remanebo. Qui vobis iubet ut faciatis, ipse nobis iubet ut loquamur. Si non faciente quod iubet ut faciatis, adversarii eius estis; non dicendo quod iubet ut dicamus, adversarii eius remanebimus. CAPUT IV.—4. Numquid in ceteris, quae supra dixi, multis immoratus sum? Hoc enim praesumimus of Caritate vestra, quia unum Deum colitis. Hoc praesumimus de fide catholica, quae in vobis est, quia Filium Dei aequalem creditis Patri: nec in vanum accipitis nomen Domini Dei vestri, ut putetis creaturam esse Filium Dei. Quoniam omnis creatura vanitati subiecta est (Rom 8:20). Sed creditis cum aequalem Patri esse, Deum de Deo, Verbum apud Deum, Verbum Deum, per quod facta sunt omnia, lumen de lumine, coaeternum illi qui genuit, unum cum illo qui genuit; et hoc Verbum creditis assumpsisse creaturam, de virgine Maria assumpsisse mortalitatem, et passum Fuisse pro nobis: ea legimus, et credimus, ut salvemur. Nec in eo immoratus sum, ut quidquid facitis, pro spe Future faciatis. Novi enim omnium Christianorum minds of saeculo

For he who does not think about the future century, and did not become a Christian hoping to finally receive what God promised, is not yet a Christian. Nor have I stopped at the sentence of God that says: Honor your father and your mother. Because many honor their parents, and we rarely find parents who complain about the ingratitude of their children, although they are not lacking either; The rarer the sin, the less it should be insisted upon. Nor did I stop to explain: Thou shalt not kill. I don't think there is a mob of murderers here. On the other hand, the serpent has widely taken hold of that other evil, and in it that adversary who shouts with the intention of becoming a friend is vehemently irritated. Every day there are conflicts, although the wives themselves no longer dare to complain about their husbands. Thus, instead of the law, a custom is observed that invades everything, so that the women themselves are already convinced that this is lawful for men, not for women. They hear that some have been taken to court because they were caught with their servants, but they have never heard of a man being taken to court for being caught with his maid, although the sin is the same. Sin being equal, it makes the man seem more innocent; not before the divine truth, but before human perversity. Perhaps someone has had to put up with his slightly demanding wife, who spoke more freely; He had believed that this was lawful for men, but he has heard in the church that it is not lawful; perhaps that guy, upon hearing his wife complaining more freely and reproaching him: "It's not a future cogitare." Qui enim non de futur saeculo cogitat, nec propterea christianus est, ut id quod in fine Deus promittit, accipiat, nondum christianus est. Ñeque in eo immoratus sum, ubi dicit sermo Dei, Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam. Multi enim honorant patents, et rato invenimus parentes conquerentes de improbitate filiorum; quamvis non desint: sed tamen quam rare fit, tam breviter monendum Fuit. Nec in eo ubi dictum est, Non occides, immorari volui: non enim credo esse hic turbam homicidarum. Illud vero malum late serpens plus occupavit, et in eo vehementius irritatur adversarius ille, qui ideo clamat, ut sit aliquando amicus. Querelae quotidianae sunt, quanquam ipsae feminae iam nec audent conqueri de viris suis. Ita invadens omnia consuetudo pro lege observatur, ut iam et mulieribus forte persuasum sit, licere hoc viris, non licere mulieribus.

Solent enim audire adductas mulieres esse ad forum, quae forte cum servís inventae sunt: adductum virum ad forum, quia inventus est cum ancilla sua, nunquam audierunt; cum sit par peccatum. In sin pari innocentiorem facit videri virum, non divina veritas, sed humano perversitas. Et si forte hodie acriorem quisquam passus fuerit uxorem suam, et liberius murmurantem, cui iam vídebatur quia licebat viro, et audivit in Ecclesia quia non licet viro: si ergo passus fuerit uxorem suam liberius iam, ut dixi, murmurantem, et dicentem sibi, Non licet quod facis; simul audimus, christiani sumus, quod a me

what you do is lawful. Together we have heard it. We are Christians. What you demand of me, keep it for me. If I owe you fidelity, you also owe it to me, and we both owe it to Christ. And if you deceive me, are you not deceiving him of whom we belong, are you not deceiving him who redeemed us? When this guy hears these or similar things, since he doesn't want to be cured, he turns against me. He gets angry and curses. And perhaps he even says: "Why did this preacher come or why did my wife come here today?" I think he says it in his thoughts, because he won't dare say it out loud even in front of his only wife. Perhaps, if he vents and says that, she may respond, saying: “Why do you curse the one you recently praised? Without a doubt we are spouses. And if you create discord with your tongue, how can you live according to me? 4 I, brothers, attend to your danger, not to your whim. If the doctor attends to the patient's will, he will never cure him. What should not be done, should not be done. What God forbids, do not do. Whoever believes in God, let him say what I say. Without a doubt, for many who do not want to correct themselves, it was better that I had not come here, if I was going to say this, or that I had not said it, since I have already come. 5. I remember that the day before yesterday I said 5 to your holiness that if I were a cytar player, or exhibited some similar popular art, according to the desires of your frivolity, from which I try to separate you, you would retain me so that I could appoint you a day, and each one, according to his or her possibilities, would offer me his contribution. you demand, redde mihi: fidem tibi debeno, fidem mihi deben, fidem Christo ambo debenmus; et if you fail me, non fallís eum cuius sumus, non fallís eum qui nos emit. Haec atque huiusmodi audiens ille, quae non solet, dum non vult in se fieri sanus, in me fit insanus, irascitur, maledicít: fortassis etiam dicat, Quomodo fac[79]tum est ut huc ille vinoet, aut uxor mea ipso die in ecclesiam proceedet? Et hoc credo quod in cogitatione sua dicat: nam libere erumpere in vocem non audet, nec ante solam uxorem suam. Fortassis enim si eruperit, et hoc dixerit, potest illa respondé, et dicere: Quare maledicis, cui paulo ante acclamabas? Certe coniuges sumus: cum lingua tua discordas, mecum concorditer quomodo vivere poteris? Nos, fratres, pericula vestra intuemur, non voluntates vestras attendimus: nam et medicus si voluntatem aegri attendat, nunquam illum curat. Quod non est faciendum, non fiat: quod prohibet Deus, non fiat.

Qui Deo credit, ab ipso audit quod dicimus. Certe melius erat quibusdam nolentibus corrigi, ut vel huc non vinoremus, si ista dicturi eramus; vel quia iam venimus, non ea diceremus. 5. Nudiustertiano die memini me dixisse Sanctitati vestrae, quia si citharoedi essemus, aut huiusmodi aliquid populariter exhibitantes pro studiis nugacitatis vestrae, quae iam quaesumus ut relinquatis, tenuissetis nos,

Why would we spend our time delighting in vain songs that are of no use, sweet in the moment and bitter in the long run? The human spirit, attracted by the clumsiness of such songs, becomes enervated, declines in virtue and slides into clumsiness. And because of those clumsinesses he then feels pain and with intense bitterness he digests what he drank with temporary sweetness. That's why it's better that I sing bitter songs for you at the moment that are sweet for you later. And I do not ask you for another payment, but that you do what I tell you; or rather, don't do it because I said so. He who fears no one says it to all of you and who makes me, in his name and for the glory of his mercy, fear no one either. We have all heard it, let us all act well, let us all agree with our adversary. 6. Suppose I were a cytar player. What else could I sing to you? Look, I carry the psaltery, which has ten strings. You just sang it when I started to speak, because you were my chorus. Did you not sing: O God, I will sing to you a new song, with the ten-stringed psaltery I will chant? Now I pluck the ten strings. Why is the voice of God's psalter bitter? Let us all sing with the ten-stringed psaltery. I do not sing anything that does not concern your works. In fact, the decalogue of the law has ten commandments. These ten commandments are distributed in such a way that three belong to God and seven to men. I already cited the three that belong to God: Our God is unique, we must make no image,

and we must not commit fornication against God, who is one, since Christ God, son of God, is one with the Father. Therefore, we should not take his name in vain, thinking that he was made, that is, that he is a creature through whom God made all things. But since there is only one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, we are promised eternal rest in the Holy Spirit, that is, in the gift of God. We have already received his deposit, for thus says the Apostle: He has given us the Spirit as a pledge. If we have received the pledge to begin in our God and Lord to be calm, to be meek in our God, to be patient in our God, also in him, whose pledge we have received, we will be forever rested. That will be the Saturday of Saturdays, for the rest that concerns the gift of the Holy Spirit. Let us, then, spiritually recognize that third commandment of the Sabbath of which we speak and which the Jews celebrate carnally. Because it is called the Holy Spirit, God sanctified the seventh day when he created all his works, as we read written in Genesis: God rested from all his works. God did not remain weary so that he could say: God rested from his works, but with that word he promised rest to you, who work. And since he made all things extremely excellent, God rested, says, so that you may understand that you too, after your good works, will rest and rest without end. Everything that was previously said, that is, all the other previous days, had their evening, but on the seventh day, on which God sanctified the rest, already

ut daremus vobis diem, et quisque pro modulo suo conferret nobis mercedem. Quare ambularemus delectad vanis canticis nulli rei profuturis, ad tempus dulcibus, in posterum amaris? Talibus etenim turpitudinibus cantionum animi hutnani illecti enervantur, et decidunt a virtute, defluentes in turpitudinem; et propter ipsas turpitudines postea felt pain, et cum magna amaritudine digest quod cum dulcedine temporali bíberunt. Melius ergo nos amara vobis cantamus ad tempus, quae postea dulcecant in vobis. Nec mercedem aliquam exigimus, nisi ut faciatis quae dicimus: immo non faciatis, si nos dicimus: si autem ómnibus ille dicit, qui neminem timet, et per quem fit in nomine ipsius et in gloria misericordiae ipsius, ut et nos neminem timeamus; omnes audimus, omnes faciamus, omnes cum nostro adversary concordemus. 6. Putate me citharoedum esse; quid vobis possum amplius canere? Ecce psalterium fero, decem chordas habet: hoc vos paulo ante cantastis, antequam inciperem loqui; chorus meus vostis. CAPOT V.—Nonne vos paulo ante cantastis, Deus, canticum novum sang tibí, in psalterio decem chordarum psallam tibí (Ps 143,9)? Ipsas decem chordas percussion mode. Quare amara est vox psalterii Dei? Psallam tibí in psalterio decem chordarum. Non vobis hoc canto, quod vos non faciatis. Decalogus enim Legis decem praecepta habet: quae decem praecepta sic sunt distributa, ut tria pertineant ad Deum, septem pertineant ad nomines. Tria ad Deum, quae iam said: Unus est Deus noster, the

nullam similarityinem debenmus faceré, et non fornican post Deum, qui unus est: quia Deus et Christus Filius Dei unum est cum [80] Patre. Et ideo non debent a nobis accipi in vanum, ut putemus eum factum, id est, creaturam aliquam, per quem facta sunt omnia: quia ipse unus Deus, Pater est et Filius et Spiritus sanctus. In Spiritu sancto, hoc est, in dono Dei, requies nobis sempiterna promittitur. Inde moda pignus accepimus. Sic enim dicit Apostolus: Qui dedit nobis pignus Spiritum (2 Cor 1,22). Si pignus accepimus, ut incipiamus in Domino et in Deo nostro tranquilli esse, ut simus in Deo nostro mites, simus in Deo patientes; erimus etiam in illo unde pignus accepimus, in aeternum quieti; quod erit sabbatum sabbatorum, propter ipsam requiem pertinent ad donum Spiritus sancti. Tertium itaque praeceptum de sabbato, quod diximus, quod carnaliter ludae celebrant, nos spiritualiter agnoscamus. Nam quia Spiritus sanctus dicitur, propterea septimum diem sanctificavit Deus, quando fecit omnia opera sua, sicut in Genesi scriptum legimus. Non ibi habes nominatam sanctificationem, nisi illo die ubi dicitur, Requievit Deus ab operibus suis. Non enim fatiguetus erat Deus, ut diceretur, Requievit Deus ab operibus suis (Gen 2,3): sed in illo verbo tibi laboranti requiem promisit; ut quia fecit omnia bona valde, et sic dicitur, Requievit Deus, intellegas etiam te post bona opera requieturum, et sine fine requieturum. Nam omnia superiora quae dicta sunt, id est, dies superiors habent vesperam: septimus iste dies non habet vesperam, ubi Deus sanctificavit requiem. Dicitur

He doesn't have his afternoon. It is said there: "and it was tomorrow", to begin that day; But we no longer say "and it was late" for the day to end, but rather we say: "and it was morning" for the beginning of an endless day. Thus, our rest begins with one morning, but it does not end, since we will live without ceasing. We observe the Sabbath if we act with this hope what we act. It is the third string of this decalogue, that is, the decacord of the psaltery; These commandments correspond to its three cords. 7. If we were told that you will love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul and with all your mind, and nothing was said about our neighbor, we would have not a disagreement, but a trichord. The Lord added: and you will love your neighbor as yourself. And he concluded by saying: the law and the prophets hang on these two commandments; The whole law is in those two precepts: in the love of God and in the love of neighbor. The decalogue concerns these two precepts, the love of God and the love of neighbor. Three chords correspond to the first commandment, and seven chords correspond to the other commandment, that is, love of neighbor; It is the way of life among men. That is why the number seven, in the seven strings, begins by honoring the parents, and this life takes its beginning in the union of both parents. And so, whoever does not honor his parents, who will he forgive? Honor your father and mother. And the Apostle repeats: honor your father and mother, which is the first commandment. Why is it the first, if we see that it is the fourth, but because in the nuibi, Factum est mane, ut inciperet ipse dies. Non dictum est, Factum est vespere, ut finiretur dies: sed dictum est, Factum est mane, ut ieront sine fine dies. Sic incipit ergo requies nostta, quasi mane: sed non finitur, quia in aeternum vivemus. Ad hanc spem quidquid facimus si facimus, sabbatum observamus. Ipsa est tenia chorda huius decalogi, id est, psalterii decachordi: in tribus enim chordis ad Deum pertinent praecepta. CAPUT VI.—7. Si diceretur nobis, Diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, et ex tota anima tua, et ex tota mente tua, et de proxima nostro nihil diceretur, non esset decachordum, sed trichordum. Quia. vero addidit Dominus, Et diliges proximum tuum tanquam te ipsum; et contexuit dices, In his duobus praeceptis all Lex pendet et Prophetae (Mt 22,37-40): all Lex in duobus praeceptis est, in dilectione Dei et dilectione proximi; ad duo itaque praecepta, id est, ad dilectionem Dei et proximi pertinet decalogus.

Ad primum praeceptum tres chordae pertinent, quia Deus est Trinitas. Ad alterum vero praeceptum, id est, ad dilectionem proximi, septem chordae: quomodo vivatur inter homines. Nam ipse numerus septenarius, tanquam septem chordarum, incipit ab honore parentum: Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam (Ex 22,12). Ad parentes enim suos [81] homo aperít oculos, et haec vita ab eorum amicitia sumit exordium. Quisquís autem suis parentibus non defert honorem, quibus parere poterit? Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam. Et dicit Apostplus; Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam, quod est man-
The ten commandments and the ten-stringed lyre

Mere seven is the first? For the love of neighbor it is the first of the second table. That is why two tables of the law were given. God gave his servant Moses on the mountain two tables of stone on which the ten commandments of the law were written, and this is the psaltery of ten strings; three on one table belonged to God, seven on the other referred to our neighbor. And in that second table the first was: honor your father and your mother. The second: you will not fornicate. The third: you will not kill. The fourth: you shall not steal. The fifth: you will not bear false witness. The sixth: you will not desire your neighbor's wife. The seventh: you will not desire your neighbor's property. Let us add these to the first three, which referred to the love of God, if we want to sing a new song with the ten-stringed psaltery. 8. Pay attention to your charity so that I can tell you what the Lord suggests to me. The Jewish people received the law, but did not observe these commandments of the decalogue. Whoever kept them did so out of fear of punishment, not out of love of justice. He held the psaltery, but he did not sing. Pleasure is for the one who sings; fatigue, for him who fears. The old man, or does not act VL acts out of fear, not out of love for holiness; not for the joy of chastity, not for the temperance of charity, but for fear. He is an old man, and the old man can sing an old song, not a new song. To sing a new song you have to be a new man. And how can he be a new man? Listen not to me, but to the Apostle, who says: strip yourselves of the datum primum (Eph 6,2). How primum, when quartum est mandatum, nisi quia in septenario number est primum? Ad dilectionem proximi primum est in altera tabula. Nam ideo duae tabulae Legis datae sunt. Deus enim fámulo suo Moysi in monte duas tabulas dedit, in quibus duabus tabulis lapidéis conscripta erant decem praecepta Legis (Ex 31,18) (quod est psalterium decem chordarum); tria in una tabula ad Deum pertinentia, septem in alter tabula ad proximum. In altera ergo tabula primum est, Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam. Secundum, Non moechaberis. Tertium, Non occides. Quartum, Non furaberis. Quintum, Non falsum testimonium you say. Sextum, Non concupisces uxorem proximi tui. Septimum, Non concupisces rem proximi tui. Haec iungamus illis tribus ad dilectionem Dei pertinentibus (ib., 20,1-17), si in psalterio decem chordarum volumus cantore canticum novum. CAPUT VIL—8. Attendat enim Caritas vestra, ut dicam quod Dominus suggerit.

Accepit Legem populus Iudaeorum istam in decalogue: non observavit. Et quicumque obtemperabant, timore obtemperabant poenae, non amore iustitiae: portabant psalterium, non cantabant. Cantanti enim voluptas est, timenti onus est. Ideo vetus homo aut non facit, aut timore facit; non amore sanctitatis, non delectatione castitatis, temperantiae, caritatis, sed timore. Vetus enim homo est; et vetus homo canticum vetus cantore potest, non novum. Ut autem cantet canticum novum, sit novus homo. Quomodo autem possit esse novus homo, audi, non me,

old man and put on the new. And so that by saying, put off the old man and put on the new, no one thinks that he has to put on something and receive something when he is told to change his man, he added: therefore, putting away the lie, speak the truth. That means strip off the old man and put on the new. It means: Change your habits. You loved the century, love God; You loved the trifles of iniquity, the temporal joys, now love your neighbor. If you do it for love, you sing a new song. If you do it out of fear, but you do it, you already hold the psaltery, but you still do not sing. And if you don't even do it, you have thrown away the same psaltery. It is better to carry it than to throw it away. But it is also better to sing at ease than to sustain it with fatigue. Whoever carries it with fear is still in his old man. Pay attention now, brothers, to what I tell you. He will not agree with his adversary who still works out of fear. He fears that God will come and condemn him. He still does not like chastity, he does not delight in justice, but he refrains from acting because he fears the judgment of God. He does not condemn the very concupiscence that boils in him. He does not delight in what is good. He does not feel like singing the new song, but fears the punishments for his old age. He has not come to an agreement with his adversary. 9. These subjects are frequently overcome by a certain thought with which they say to themselves: "If it could be, God should not

threaten us, say things through his prophets that terrify men, but he should come to offer forgiveness to everyone, to forgive everyone; come, yes, but without sending anyone to hell. Since he is wicked, he wants God to be wicked too. God wants to make you like him, and you insist on making God like you. May God be grateful to you as he is and not as you want him to be. You are perverse and you want a God as you are, not as he is. If you like him as he is, you will correct yourself and direct your heart to that rule, from which you are now strange and crooked. Be grateful to God for who he is, love him for who he is. He does not love you as you are, but hates you as you are. He feels sorry for you because he hates you for who you are, to make you who you are not yet. Become God, I say, who you are not yet. He still doesn't promise you that he will make you what he is. You will be as he is, but in a certain way, that is, an imitator of God, like his image, but not like the image that is his Son. The images are also different among men. A son bears the image of his father and is the same as his father, because he is a man like his father. On the other hand, in a mirror, your image is not the same as you. Your image in your child is one thing and another in the mirror. In the son is your image according to the equality of the substance; On the other hand, in the mirror, how different it is in substance! However, there is a certain image of you, although it is not as it is given in the son according to the substance. Thus, the image of God is not the same in the creature as in the Son, who is the same as the Father, that is, God, Word of God, through whom he created all things. Receive, then,

sed Apostolum dicentem, Exuite, vos, veterem hominem, et induite novum. Et ne quis putaret, cuín dixit, Exuite, vos, veterem hominem, et induite novum; alíquid deponendum esse et aliquid accipiendum, cum de imitando praeciperet nomine, subiecit et ait, Quapropter deponentes mendacium, loquimini veritatem (Eph 4,22-25). Hoc est quod ait, Exuite veterem hominem, et induite novum: hoc dixit, Mutate mores. Saeculum diligebatis, Deum diligite: nugatoria iniquitatis, temporalis voluptates diligebatis; proximum diligite. Si dilectione facitis, canticum novum cantatis: si timore facitis, facitis tamen; portatis quidem psalterium, sed nondum cantatis: si autem nec hoc facitis, proicitis ipsum psalterium. Melius est vel portare, quam proicere: sed rursus, melius cum voluptate cantore, quam cum onere portare. Nec pervenit ad canticum novum, nisi iam cum voluptate cantans. Nam qui portat cum timore, adhuc in vetustate est. Et quid est quod dico, fratres, attendite. Non concordavit [82] cum adversa suo, qui cum timore adhuc facit: timet enim ne veniat Deus, et damnet illum. Nam nondum delectat castitas, nondum illum delectat iustitia; sed iudicium Dei formidans, a factis temperat: non concupiscentiam ipsam damnans, quae saevit in eo. Nondum illum delectat quod bonum est: nondum ibi habet suavitatem, ut cantet canticum novum; thirst for vetustate poenas timet: nondum concordavit cum adversary. CAPUT VIII.—9. Such enim homines, plerumque supplantantur tali cogitatione, ut dicant sibi: Si fieri posset, non nobis minaretur Deus, non

talia per Prophetas suos diceret, quae homines deterrerent; sed antequam vinoret, daret omnibus indulgentiam, ignosceret omnibus, postea vinoret, neminem mitteret in gehennas. Iam quia iniquus est, iniquum vult Deum. Vult te Deus faceré similem sui, et conaris tu Deum faceré similem tui. Placeat tibi ergo Deus qualis est, non qualem illum esse vis. Perversus enim es, et talem vis Deum qualis es, non qualis est. Si autem placeat tibi qualis est, corregeris, et directes in eam regulam cor tuum, a qua nunc alienus distortus es. Placeat tibi Deus qualis est, ama qualis est: non te ipse amat qualis es, sed odit te qualis es. Ideo tui miseretur, quia odit te qualis es, ut faciat te qualis nondum es. Faciat te, dixi, qualis nondum es. Nam illud tibi non promittit, quia faciet te qualis est. Nam eris qualis est, sed ad quemdam modum; Id est, imitator Dei velut imago, sed non qualis imago est Filius. Nam etiam imagines in hominibus diversee sunt. Filius hominis habet imaginem patris sui, et hoc est quod pater eius, quia homo est sicut pater eius. In speculo autem imago tua non hoc est quod tu. Aliter est enim imago tua in filio, aliter in speculo: in filio est imago tua secundum aequalitatem substantiae; in speculo autem quantum longe est a substantia, et tamen est quaedam imago tua, quamvis non talis, qualis in filio tuo secundum substantiam. Sic in creature, non hoc est imago Dei, quod est in Filio, qui hoc est quod Pater, id est, Verbum Dei per quod facta sunt omnia. Recipe ergo similarityinem Dei, quam per

the likeness of God, which you lost through your evil works. The image of the emperor is different on the coin and on the son, since both are images; but that of the currency is printed and different. For just as the image of the emperor is different in the son and in the gold doubloon 6, so you are the coin of God; and you are better, because you are a coin with intelligence and a certain life so that you know whose image you hold, in whose image you were created, because the doubloon does not know that it bears the image of the king. Thus, as I had begun to say, God hates you as you are, but loves you as he wants you to be; That is why he exhorts you to convert. Agree with him and begin, above all, to love yourself well and hate yourself just as you are. This is the beginning of agreement with the word of God, starting to hate yourself as you are. When you have begun to hate yourself as you are and as God hates you, you begin to love God as he is. 10. Look at a sick person. When a sick person hates his illness as he is, he begins to agree with the doctor. Because the doctor hates him for who he is. That's why she wants him healthy, because she hates him being feverish; The doctor is a persecutor of fever to be a liberator of man. Thus are the fevers of your soul: greed, libido, hatred, concupiscence, lust, the frivolity of spectacles. You must hate them with the doctor. By agreeing with the doctor, you will strive with the doctor, you will listen with pleasure to what the doctor orders; you will do with bad facta amisisti. Sicut enim in nummo imago imperatoris aliter est, aliter in filio: nam imago et imago est; sed aliter impressa est in nummo, aliter in filio, aliter in solido aureo imago imperatoris: sic et tu nummus Dei es, ex hoc melior, quia cum intellectu et cum quadam vita nummus Dei es, ut scias etiam cuius imaginem geras, et ad cuius imaginem factus sis: nam nummus nescit se habere imaginem imperatoris. Ergo ut dicere coeperam, odit te Deus qualis es, sed amat te taíem qualem te esse vult: et ideo Ule te ut muteris hortatur. Concorda cum illo, et incipe primo bene velle, et odisse te qualis es: hoc sit tibi initium concordiae cum sermone Dei, ut inopias primo tu odisse te qualis es. Cum coeperis et tu odisse te talem qualis es, sicut te talem odit Deus, incipis iam ipsum directere Deum qualis est. [83] 10. Aegrum attendite. Aeger aegrotantem se odit qualis est: inde incípít concordare cum medico.

Quia et medicus odit eum qualis est: nam ideo vult sanum esse, quia odit eum febrientem: et est medicus febris persecutor, ut sit hominis liberator. Sic avaritia, sic libido, sic odium, concupiscentia, luxuria, sic nugacitas spectaculorum, febres sunt animae tuae, deben illas odisse cum medico: ita concordas cum medico, niteris cum medico, et libenter audis quod iubet medicus, libenter facís The solidus aureus is a coin whose value was from the time of Constantine of 1/72 part of the Roman gold pound.

I like what the doctor commands, and as your health progresses, his commandments will begin to please you. How heavy* food is for the sick when he has to nourish himself! Women believe that eating time is worse than attack time. And, nevertheless, they are forced to agree with the doctor, and, although reluctantly and by force, they prevail to take something. How eagerly will they accept greater things when they are healthy, when when they are sick they accept the lesser precepts? Why does it happen like this? Because they hated their fever, because they agreed with the doctor and together the doctor and the patient persecuted the fever. In the same way, when I say that, I only hate your fevers, or rather, in me the word of God hates your fevers, with which you must agree. For what am I, but one who is to be delivered and healed with you? 11. Do not look at me, but look at the Word of God. Don't be angry with your medicine; I couldn't find anywhere else to go. I reached the fifth string as a man when playing the ten-string psaltery. Was I going to ignore the fifth? On the contrary, he had to press harder; Since I see that almost the entire human race falls into it, I see that we have to work more. And when I press it, what do I say? Do not commit adultery against your wives, for you do not want that; they commit it against you. Don't go where you don't want them to follow you. Without cause you try to excuse yourself when you say: "Do I mess with someone else's wife? "I'm just looking for my maid." quod iubet medicus, et proficiente iam sanitate incipiunt etiam delectare praecepta. Quam onerosus est cibus aegris quando reficiuntur: et peiorem horam deputant aegri refectionis suae, quam suae accessionís; et tamen cogunt se concordantes cum medico, et quamvis inviti et obluctantes vincunt se ut aliquid accipiant. Quanta aviditate sani maiora percepturí sunt, unde aegri minora vix accipiunt? Sed unde hoc factum est? Quias oderant febrem suam, et cum medico concordaverunt, et simul persequebantur febrem medicus et aegrotus. Cum ergo et nos talia dicimus, non odimus nisi febres vestras: immo in nobis ipse sermo Dei febres dressas odit, cum quo concordare debentis. Nam nos quid sumus, nisi liberandi vobiscum, sanandi vobiscum? HOOD IX.—11. Modo non me intueamini, sed sermonem Dei. Nolite irasci vestro medicine; non inveni enim aliud qua tranirem.

Come ad quintam chordam homo, qui tango psalterium decem chordarum; numquid praetermissurus eram quintam? Immo assidue percussurus. In illa enim video iacere totum penis genus humanum, in illa video plus laborare. Ipsam striking the crux? Nolite moechari post uxores vestras, quia non vultis ut moechentur post vos uxores vestras. Nolite iré vos, quo eas sequi non vultis. Sine causa vos excusare conamini, quando dicitis:: Numquid eo ad uxorem alienam? Ad ancillam meam eo. Vis ut dicat

Do you want your wife to tell you: "Am I looking for someone else's husband? "I'm just looking for my servant." You say: "It is not a foreign woman I am looking for." Perhaps you want them to tell you: "It is not a foreign husband that I am looking for." I hope she doesn't tell you that. It will be better to regret you than to imitate you. She is chaste, a holy woman and a true Christian who regrets her fornicating husband, and does not grieve for the flesh, but for charity, and does not regret your adultery because she does not commit it, but because it is harmful to you. Because if he stops committing it so that you don't commit it, he will commit it if you commit it. On the other hand, if what you demand from her she owes to God, she owes it to Christ, and she is faithful to you because God commands it, even if her husband fornicates, she will offer her chastity to God. Because Christ speaks in the hearts of good women, he speaks inside, where the husband does not hear, since he is not worthy to hear if he is a fornicator. So she speaks inwardly and consoles her daughter by saying these words: “Do your husband's insults hurt you? So what has he done to you? Regret him, but do not imitate him in doing evil, but let him imitate you in doing good. In that he does wrong, do not consider him as your head, but rather me. Because, if he is the head in his evil work, the body will follow his head and both will go to the precipice. In order not to follow your bad head, stick to the head of the Church, which is Christ. Owing chastity to him, offering him her honor, whether her husband is present or absent, she will not sin, since the one to whom she owes will never be absent in order not to sin.

12. Do this, my brothers, so that you can agree with your adversary. What I tell you is not bitter, or if it is bitter, it must be medicinal. Take the drink even if it is bitter. It is bitter because the insides are in danger: you have to drink it. Better will be a little bitterness in the jaws than eternal torment in the bowels. Convert, then. Those of you who did not practice this good of chastity, practice it. Do not say: "It is impossible." It is ugly, my brothers, it is clumsy for a man to say that what a woman does is impossible. It is criminal for a man to say: "I can't." What a woman can do, can't a man do? How, doesn't she carry the meat? She was seduced by the snake the first. Your chaste wives show you that what you do not want to do is possible, what you say is impossible. Perhaps you say that she can do it more easily because she is kept under greater surveillance: the precept of the law, the surveillance of her husband, the terror of public laws 7. There is also a strong support of modesty and modesty. But if so many providences make the woman more chaste, let the same virility make the husband chaste. Women are monitored more because their weakness is greater. If she blushes before her husband, don't you blush before Christ? You are freer because you are stronger. Because you win easily they leave you free. The husband's diligence, the terror of the laws, social custom and modesty are reserved for her. For you God, only God. You easily find other men equal to you, before whom you do not have to be ashamed, since there are many who do wrong.

uxor tua tibi: Numquid eo ad virum alienum? Ad servum meum eo. You say: Non est uxor aliena, ad quam vado. Numquid vis dicatur tibi: Non est vir alienus, ad quem vado? Absit ut dicat hoc illa. Melius enim dolet te, quam imitatur te. Illa enim casta et sancta femina et veré christiana, quae dolet fornicantem virum, et non dolet propter carnem, sed dolet propter caritatem; non ideo non vult ut facias, quia et ipsa non facit, sed quia tibi non expedit. Nam si propterea non facit, ut tu non facias; si feceris, faciet. Si autem Deo illud debeat, si Christo illud debeat quod tu exigís, et ideo reddet, quia iubet ille; etsi fornicatur vir, castitatem femina illa Deo exhibitat. Christus enim loquitur in cordibus bonarum feminatum, loquitur intus ubi non audít vir, quia nec dignus est, si talis est: loquitur ergo ille interius, et dicit, et filiam suam consolatur huiusmodi verbis: De iniuriis viri tui torqueris, quid tibi enim fecit? Dole; sed ipsum noli imitari, ut male facias, sed ipse te imitatetur in bono. Nam ín eo quod male facit, noli eum putare caput [84] tuum, sed me Deum tuum. Nam si et in eo quod male facit caput est, et secuturum est Corpus caput suum; eunt both per praeceps. Ut autem non sequatur malum caput suum, teneat se ad caput Ecclesiae Christum: huic debens castitatem suam, huic deferens honorem suum, absens sit vir, praesens sit vir, non peccat illa; quia nunquam est absens, cui debent ut

12. Haec ergo, fratres mei, facite, ut possitis concordare cum adversary. Nec amara sunt quae dico; aut si amara sunt, curant. Potio ista si amara est, accipiatur: quia in periculo sunt viscera, amara est, bibatur. Melius est modica amaritudo in faucibus, quam aeternum tormentum in visceribus. Mutate yourself. Quicumque non faciebatis hoc bonum castitatis, iam facite. Nolite dicere: Non potest fieri. Foedum est, fratres mei, turpe est, ut vir dicat non posse fieri quod facit femina. Scelus est, ut vir dicat: Non possum. Quod potest femina, vir non potest? Quid enim, illa carnem non portat? Prior to serpente decepta est. Castae uxores vestrae ostendunt vobis fieri posse quod non vultis faceré, et dicitis fieri non posse! Be strong you say, ideo illam facilius faceré posse, quia plana illi custodia est, legis praeceptum, diligentia maritalis, terror etiam legum publicum; est etiam verecundiae et Pudoris illius magnum munimentum. Multae custodiae faciunt feminam castiorem, virum castum faciat ipsa virilitas. Nam ideo mulieri maior custody, quia maior infirmitas. Illa erubescit viro, tu non erubescis Christo? Your liberior, quia fortior: quia facile vincis, ideo tibi commissus es. Super illam et diligentia viri, et terror legum, et consuetudo morum, et verecundia maior: et Deus super te, tantum Deus. Invenís enim facile pairs viros, quibus non timeas

Such is the perversity of the human race, that sometimes we have to fear more that the chaste will be ashamed among the shameless 8. That is why I do not stop plucking this fifth string, due to the perverse custom and vice of the entire human race, as I have said. If someone among you commits murder, God forbid, you want to throw him out of the country and expel him immediately if possible. If someone commits a robbery, you hate him and you don't want to see him. If anyone bears false testimony, you abhor him and he does not seem like a man to you. If someone desires other people's goods, you consider him a thief and unjust. But if someone sins with their servants, they are loved, they are received with flattery, the wounds become graces. And if there is someone who says that he is chaste, that he does not commit adultery and it is known that he does not commit it, he is afraid to approach those who commit it so that they do not insult him, so that they do not laugh at him and say that he is not a man. Human perversity stoops to such an extent that he who is overcome by libido is called a man and he who conquers libido is not considered a man. Those who triumph, celebrate the triumph and are not men; and, on the other hand, those who lie prostrate are men. If you went to see the amphitheater, did you expect to consider the one who lies felled by the beast stronger than the one who felled the beast? 13. But since you ignore the internal struggle and delight in external strife, you do not want to belong to the new song, in which it is said: whoever guides my hands in the struggle and my erubescere, quia faciunt illud multi. Et tanta est perversitas genetis humani, ut aliquando metuendum sit ne castus erubescat inter impudicos. Ideo non cesso tangere quintam istam chordam, propter ipsam perversam consuetudinem et labem totius, ut dixi, generis humani. Si quis inter vos faciat homicidium, quod avertat Deus, pellere illum vultis de patria, et continuo, si fieri potest, excludere. Si quis faciat furtum, odistis illum, nec videre vultis. Si quis dicat falsum testimonium, abominamini, nec vobis homo videtur. Si quis concupiscat alienas res, raptor et iniustus deputatur. Si quis volutatur cum ancillis suis, amatur, brandish accipitur; convertuntur vulnera in ioca. Si quis autem existat qui dicat se castum, non faceré adulterium, notum autem sit quod non faciat; erubescit accessé ad illos non sui similes, ne insultent, ne irrideant, ne dicant non esse virum. Ad hoc delapsa est humano perversitas, ut vir habeatur victus a libídine, et vir non habeatur victor líbidinis.

Triumphantes exsultant, et non sunt viri: iacent prostrati, et viri sunt? Si spectares, ille tibi videretur fortior, qui íaceret sub bestiam, quam qui perimeret bestiam? [851 13. Sed quia dissimulatis a struggle interiore, et delectant vos struggle exteriors, ideo non vultis pertinere ad canticum novum; ubi These words recall those others from the Confessions: "I felt ashamed of being less shameless than those, and I liked to do evil not only for the pleasure of committing it, but also to be praised" (II 3,7).

fingers in war. There is a war that man maintains with himself, fighting against evil desires, curbing greed, dominating pride, suffocating ambition, slaughtering libido. You hold these contentions in secret and are not outwardly defeated. That is why your hands are trained for fighting and your fingers for war. This does not occur among your shows. In these shows the hunter is not the same as the citar player 9; The hunter performs a different function from the citar player. In God's show it is the same. Press these ten strings and kill the beasts. You perform double duty at the same time. You press the first string, in which only one God is worshiped, and the beast of superstition falls. You press the second, in which you do not take the name of the Lord in vain, and the beast of error of the nefarious heresies, which admitted that, falls. You press the third string, on which, looking to the hope of future rest, you do what you do, and the love of this century dies, crueler than the other beasts. Indeed, for the love of this century men work in all their businesses. Work in all your good works not for the love of this world, but for the eternal rest that God promises you. See how you perform both functions at the same time: you pluck the strings and kill the beasts, and thus you are a citar player and a hunter. Do you not delight in these spectacles, in which you please not the eyes of the businessman, but those of the redeemer? Honor your father and mother: You play the fourth string, to offer honor to parents, dicitur, Qui docet manus meas ad proelium, et digits meos ad bellum (Ps 143,1). Est enim bellum quod secum agit homo, dimicans contra concupiscentias malas, frenans avaritiam, elidens superbiam, suffocans ambitionem, trucidans libidinem. Has pugnas facis in occulto, et non vinceris in aperto. Ad hoc docentur manus vestrae ad proelium, et digiti vestri ad bellum. Non est hoc in spectaculis vestris. In illis spectaculis non id est venator, quod citharista; aliud agit venator, aliud citharista: in spectaculo Dei unum est. Tange easdem decem chordas, et feras occides, utrumque simul facis. Tangís primam chordam, qua unus colitur Deus; cecidit bestia superstitionis. Tangís secundam, qua non accipit nomen Domini Dei tui in vanum; cecidit bestia erroris nefandarum haeresum, quae id putaverunt. Tangís tertiam chordam, ubi pro spe Futurae quietis facis quidquid facit; interficitur crudelior ceteris bestiis amor saeculi huius.

Propter amorem enim saeculi huius laborant homines in ómnibus negotiis: tu autem in ómnibus bonis operibus tuis labora, non propter amorem saeculi huius, sed propter sempiternam requiem quam promittit Deus. Vide quomodo utrumque simul facis, et chordas tangís, et bestias occidis, id est, et citharista es et venator. Non vos delectant talia spectacula, ubi non promeremur oculos editoris, sed oculos Redemptoris? Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam: tangis quartam chordam,

and the beast of impiety falls. You shall not fornicate: You press the fifth string and the beast of lightness falls. Thou shalt not kill: You press the sixth string and the beast of cruelty falls. You will not commit theft: You press the seventh string and the beast of rapacity falls. You shall not bear false witness: You press the eighth string and the beast of falsehood falls. You will not desire your neighbor's wife: You press the ninth string and the beast of adulterous thought falls. Because it is one thing to fornicate with another woman and another to lust after another's wife. That is why two commandments were given: You shall not commit fornication and you shall not lust after your neighbor's wife. You shall not desire your neighbor's property: You strike the tenth string and the beast of greed falls. And so, when all the beasts fall, you walk safely and innocently in the love of God and in the society of men. By pressing the ten strings, how many beasts you kill! Because under these heads there are many other heads. On each rope you kill not a single beast, but herds of beasts. And so you will sing a new song with love, not with fear. 14. Do not say to yourself when you want to do something in matters of lust: "I have no wife, I do what I want, because I do not sin against my wife." You already know your price, you know which altar you approach, what you eat and drink, or better yet, who you eat and drink. Abstain from fornication. And do not say to yourself: "I am looking for a harlot, a harlot, a prostitute, and I do not violate the precept that says: You shall not commit adultery, since I do not yet have a wife nor do anything against her; Nor do I violate that precept that says: no ut honorem parentibus deferas; cecidit bestia impietatis. Non moechaberís: tangís quintam chordam; cecidit beast libidinis. Non occides: tangis sextam chordam; cecidit beast crudelitatis. Non furtum facies: tangis septimam chordam; cecidit beast rapacitatis. Non falsum testimonium you say: tangis octavem chordam; cecidit bestia falsitatis. Non concupisces uxorem proximi tui: tangis nonam chordam; cecidit bestia adulterinae cogitationis. Aliud est enim non faceré aliquid tale praeter uxorem, aliud non appetere alienam uxorem. Ideo duo praecepta sunt, Non moechaberís, et, Non concupisces uxorem proximi tui. Non concupisces rem proximi tui: tangis decimam chordam; cecidit beast cupiditatis. Ita cadentibus omnibus bestiis securus et innocens in Dei dilectione et humano societate versaris. Tangens chordas decem, quot occidis beasts? Nam fines capita sunt sub istis capitibus. In singulis chordis non singulas bestias, sed greges interficis bestiarum.

Sic ergo canticum novum cum amore, non cum timore cantabis. CAPUT X.—14. Noli dicere tibi, quando forte luxurianter aliquid vis agere: Uxorem non habeo, fació quod voló; non enim post uxorem meam pecco. Iam nosti pretium tuum, iam nosti quo accessis, quid manduces, quid bibas: immo quem manduces, quem bibas. Abstine te a fornicationibus. Ne forte mihidicas: Ad fornicem vado, ad meretricem pergo, ad prostitutem eo: nec illud praeceptum violo, quo dictum [86] est, Non moechaberís; quia uxorem nondum habeo, nec post illam aliquid fació:

You will desire your neighbor's wife. In seeking a public woman, in what precept do I sin? Will we not find a string to pluck? Shall we not find a rope, with whose nerve we bind this fugitive? Don't run away, because there is something to tie him up with. But love, and so you won't have to tie it, but rather decorate it. In the ten strings we find the one we are looking for. In fact, the ten commandments, as we have heard, refer to those two precepts, to the love of God and neighbor, and both to one last, unique one, namely: Do not do to another what you do not want them to do to you. The ten are contained there and also the two. 15. But you say: "If I commit theft, I do what I do not want to suffer; If I kill, I do what I do not want done to me; If I do not honor my parents, I do what I do not want to suffer, by wanting my children to honor me; If I am an adulterer or commit adultery, I do what I do not want to tolerate. When we ask someone, they say, “I don't want my wife to do that; If I desire my neighbor's wife, I do not want another to desire mine; I do what I don't want to suffer; If I desire my neighbor's goods, and I do not want them to desire my own, I do what I do not want to suffer. But when I go to a prostitute: to whom do I do what I don't want to suffer? You do it to God, and that is more serious. Understand your holiness. Do not do to another what you do not want them to do to you, which concerns the two aforementioned precepts. As? If you do not do to man what you do not want man to do to you, that belongs to the commandment of your neighbor, to the love of your neighbor, nec illud praeceptum violo, ubi dictum est, Non concupisces uxorem proximi tui. Qui ad publicam vado, in quod praeceptum incurro? Non invenimus chordam, quam tangamus? non invenimus chordam? Quo nervo ligemus fugitivum istum? Non fugiat, habet unde ligetur: sed amet, et non erit ligamentum, sed ornamentum. Non enim ligamentum, sed ornatnentum in ipsis decem chordis invenimus. Decem enim praecepta ad duo illa referuntur, sicuti audivimus, ut diligamus Deum et proximum: et duo illa ad unum illud. Unum est autem, Quod tibi fieri non vis, alii ne feceris (Tob 4,16). Ibi continentur decem, ibi continentur duo. 15.

Sed dicis: Furtum si faciam, id fació quod pati nolo: si occidam, id fació quod ab altero pati nolo: si parentibus meis honorem non deferam, quando voló ut deferatur mihi a filiis meis, id fació quod pati nolo: si sim moechus et aliquid tale moliar, id fació quod pati nolo; nam si quis interrogetur, dicit, Nolo ut uxor mea tale aliquid faciat: si concupisco uxorem proximi mei, nolo quisquam concupiscat meam; id fació quod pati nolo: si concupisco rem proximi mei, nolo ut auferatur mea; id fació quod pati nolo: cum vero ad meretricem eo, cui fació quod pati nolo? Solomon's judgment
Topic: The judgment of Solomon. Date: Around 412. Place: Sinitum.

1. The book of Kings praises Solomon's admirable judgment between two women who are disputing over an infant. Thus it was written: Then two prostitutes came to King Solomon and appeared before him. And one of them said: Listen, sir, I and this woman lived, and I gave birth while she was at home. Three days after my birth, this woman also gave birth; We were together, there was no stranger with us in the house, apart from the two of us. This woman's son died one night, because she had slept on him. She got up during the night and took my son from my side, while your maidservant was sleeping, and laid him on her lap, and her dead son she laid on my lap. When I got up to breastfeed my son, I found him dead; But looking at him in the morning, I saw that it was not my son, the one I had given birth to. The other woman said: No, quite the opposite, my son is the living one and your son is the dead one. Vero the other replied: No, your son is the dead one and my son is the living one. And they argued before the king. The king spoke: You say: this is my son, the living one; Hers is the dead one, there is another reply: No, my son is the living one; hers is the dead one. SERMO

Et mulier said illa alia: 'Non, sed filius meus est qui vivit, filius autem tuus qui mortuus est. Et ipsa dixit: Non, filius tuus est Ule mortuus, et meus filius est qui vivit. The king said: Bring me a sword. They brought a sword before the king. The king said: Divide the living child in two and give one half to one and the other to the other. The woman whose child was alive spoke to the king, because her heart was moved for her son, and she said: Please, my lord, let them give him the child alive and do not kill him. But the other said: It will not be for me or for you; Let them break it. The king answered: Give her the living child and do not kill him: she is the mother. In this judgment the admirable prudence of the king stands out, granted by a divine gift. It was neither decorous nor appropriate to think that the mother of the child was other than the one who conceived him in a certain way again, when she saw that he had been taken away from her, and gave birth to him again by defending him from the false mother, and gave birth to him again by not allowing himself to be killed. But the ancient divine books usually not only attest to a real event, but also hint at a figure of another future event; That is why we wonder if these two women offer us something in meaning and figure. 2. At first glance it occurs to us to think that these two women are the Synagogue and the Church. For we see that the Synagogue killed Christ, their son, born of the Jews according to the flesh, sleeping, that is, following the light of the present life, without understanding the manifestation of the truth in the words of the Lord. Furthermore, it is written: Arise, you who sleep, levanqui vivit, et filius eius mortuus est; et tu dicis, Non, sed filius meus vivit, et filius eius mortuus est. Et ait Rex: Afferte mibi machaeram. Et obtulerunt ei machaeram in conspectu Regis. And say Rex: Dividite puerum qui vivit, in two parts, and date dimidium eius huic, et dimidium eius huic. Et respondedit mulier cuius erat filius qui vivebat, et dixit ad Regem, quoniam conturbata est vulva eius super filio suo; et dixit: Animadvertite, domine, date ei puerum, et nolite eum morte afficere. Et haec dixit: Ñeque mihi, ñeque huic sit, sed dividete illum. Et respondit Rex, et dixit ei mulieri quae dixit, Date eum Mi, et morte nolite eum afficere; Quia haec est mater eius (3 Reg 3,16-27). Prudentia quidem Regis divino muñere concessa in hoc iudicio mirabilis eminet. Non enim decuit, aut opportitu aliam iudicare esse matrem pueri, nisi eam quae illum iterum quodam moda concepit, eum cognovit ablatum; et iterum parturivit, dum a false matre defendit; et iterum peperit, dum non permisit occidi.

Verumtamen sicut solent divini veteres Libri; non solum rei gestae fidem, sed etiamfuturae insinuare mysterium; considera est ista Scriptura, utrum nobis in duabus istis mulieribus significatum aliquid figuratumque demonstret. 2. Mulieres duae coram Salomone litigants de filio Synagoga et Ecclesia. Sacramentorum vita, Christus.—Et duae quidem feminae Synagoga et Ecclesia in prima facie considerationis oceurrunt: Synagoga enim filium suum Christum ex iudaeis secundum carnem natum occidisse convincitur dormiens, id est praesentis vitae sequendo luzm, manifestationemque veritatis in verbis Domini non intellegens: verum etiam scriptum est, Surge, qui dormís, et exsurge a mortuis, et illuminabit te Christus

come back from the dead, and Christ will enlighten you. And since there were two of them and they lived in the same house, it will not be absurd to think that, apart from circumcision and the foreskin, no other lineage of religion has been invented. In the representation of one of the women you will place the type of religion typical of the Jews, contained in the worship and law of the only God; In the representation of the other woman you must see the uncircumcised gentility, dedicated to the worship of idols. Both were prostitutes, since the Apostle says that all the Jews and Greeks were under sin. Indeed, every soul that abandons the eternity of truth and delights in earthly clumsiness, fornicates away from the Lord. As for the Church, which came from the fornication of the Gentiles, it is clear that it did not kill Christ. But we have to find out why she is also the mother of Christ. Pay attention to the Gospel and listen to the Lord who says: Whoever does the will of my Father, he is my mother, brother and sister. Where did he sleep so that, even if he didn't drown the child, the dead one could be placed on him and the living one taken away? Perhaps this means that the sacrament of circumcision had already died among the Jews, since they understood it in their carnal way; That sacrament of circumcision no longer had life among the Jews, who had put to death Christ, who is the life of all the sacraments, since in Christ what is visibly celebrated among the Jews is understood with vitality. We say, then, that some Jews tried to impose this sacrament of circumcision,

as a lifeless body, to the Gentiles who had believed in Christ, as it is written in the Acts of the Apostles. They were told that they could not be saved if they were not circumcised. They wanted to persuade them when they ignored the law, as if by placing their dead son in the darkness of the night. Such persuasion could only be of use to them when the dream of stupidity partially dominated the Church of the Gentiles. It seems that the Apostle wanted to wake her from her sleep by crying: Oh foolish Galatians! Who fascinated you? And shortly after: Are you so foolish, he says, that having begun with the spirit, you are now consumed by the flesh? As if to say: Are you so foolish that, having previously had the living and spiritual work, you let it be lost to accept someone else's death? Therefore, in another place the same Apostle says: The spirit is life through righteousness. And elsewhere it says: To know according to the flesh is death. With these and other similar voices, that mother awakens and dawns when the darkness of the law is illuminated by the word of God, that is, by Christ, who was born, that is, who spoke in Paul. He enlightened her saying: Tell me, those of you who want to be under the law, have you not heard the law? For the Scripture says that Abraham had two sons: one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman. But that of the slave was born according to nature; that of the free, by virtue of the promise. The Synagogue can now claim that the Gospel is its own and as due to it and engendered by it. That is what those Jews who felt carnally, but dared to proclaim themselves Christians, said to the Gentiles in the discussion. They said, therefore, that the Gospel had come as a debit of his justice. But it was not theirs that they did not know how to understand spiritually. Calling themselves Christians, boasting of another's title, as that woman boasted of the son she had not conceived, they dared to argue; They had eliminated the spiritual intelligence from the works of the law, as one separates the soul from the body of its works, and by extinguishing the living spirit of prophecy they were left in their carnal works without life, that is, without spiritual understanding. Furthermore, they tried to put it on the Gentiles by taking away their

Christian name, like the living son. The Apostle refutes them in such a way that he affirms that Christian grace belongs to them the less the more they appropriate it as a debt and boast that it is theirs by right of works. For to him who works, he says, the reward is not imputed as a grace, but as a debt. On the other hand, he who does not act, but believes in him who justifies the wicked, his faith is considered righteousness. Thus he excludes from the number of these those Jews who had believed rightly and retained spiritual grace alive. He affirms that these relics of the Jewish people were saved, while the crowd went to perdition. Thus at this time, he says, the relics have been saved by the election of grace. And if by grace, it is no longer by works; Otherwise, grace is not grace. Those who appropriate the reward of the Gospel as their own thing, that is, as due and paid for their works, are therefore excluded from grace, as if the Synagogue cried: Mine is the son. But they were lying. It is true that she had also received him, but by lying on him, that is, by proudly understanding, she had killed him. And even then the true mother was vigilant: she understood that by the grace of God and not by her merits 2, since she was a prostitute, the son had been granted to her, that is, the work of evangelical faith, which she desired to nourish in the bosom of her heart. In short, the Synagogue sought the glory of men in a foreign son; The Church preserved the affection of love in its own child.

to fight for the truth, to reject hypocrisy, as a false mother of the spiritual gift of the Church, that is, of the living and foreign son, without allowing her to dominate the grace granted to others since she could not keep her own. We must do this by defending and fighting, but not to the point of danger of division. Because the judge's ruling that ordered the child to be divided was not a break in unity, but rather proof of charity. Solomon's name 3, according to the Latin translation, means peaceful. Therefore, the peaceful king does not destroy the members that retain the vital spirit for their unity and harmony. By threatening he discovers the true mother, and thus, by judging, he eliminates the false one. Therefore, if that temptation occurs so that the unity of Christian grace is not divided, we have been taught to say: "Give her the child as long as he lives." Because whoever is a true mother does not seek her honor, but rather the health of her child. Wherever the child is, the sincere affection of the mother will retain him better than the usurpation of the false mother. 5. I see that these two women in the same house also mean two lineages of men in one Church; one, that of those who are dominated by simulation; another, that of those in whom authentic charity reigns. Thus, we will consider both things, dilection and simulation, as two women. Simulation fallaciously imitates dilection. The Apostle eliminates this simulation when he says: dilection without simulation. Although habimatis.—Illud autem inter both regale iudicium nihil aliud nos admonet, nisi ut pro veritate certemus, et expellamus hypocrisim tanquam falsem matrera, a spirituali Ecclesiae dono tanquam ab alieno vivo filio; nec patiamur eam dominari concessae alus gratiae, quae suam custodire non potuit. Sed hoc faciamus defenders atque cenantes non usque ad periculum divisionis. Illa enim sententia iudicis, cum iussit parvulum dividí, non est unitatis praecisio, sed probatio caritatis. Salomonis enim nomen, sicut Latini interpretantur, Pacificum est. Rex vero pacificus non dilacerat membra, quae unitate atque concordia vitalem spiritum continent: sed minando invenit matrem veram, et iudicando separat falsem. However, so that a pious widow could feed him, he made him needy. The need of a holy soul becomes abundance for a godly soul. Could not Elijah give to himself of God's mercy what he gave to that jar? You see, then, since it is clear, that from time to time the servants of God suffer need so that those who possess may be tested. However, that widow had nothing. What was left must be finished and she would die with her children. To prepare the bread she began to gather some logs, and then Elias saw her. The man of God looked at her when she was looking for the sticks. That woman was an image of the Church. Since two logs form a cross, in order to die, he sought the sign from which life would come. Sensing the mystery, Elias tells her what she heard. The old woman describes her situation to him, telling him that she expects death once she has eaten what is left. How do you understand what the Lord had said to Elijah, Go to Zarephath in Sidon, since I have sent a widow there to feed you? You already realize how God commands, not with words, but by inspiring the heart. Do we read that a prophet was sent to that woman saying: “This is what the Lord says, a hungry servant of mine is coming to you; Give him what you have, do not fear poverty, since I will return what you give him"? We do not read that such a thing was said to him. Nor do we read that an angel appeared to him in a dream and announced that Elijah would come hungry and that he must feed him.

God speaks to the heart with admirable means. We see that God commanded speaking to the heart, suggesting to the widowed woman what was necessary and persuading her of what was useful. In a similar way we read in the prophets that God commanded the worm to gnaw the root of the gourd. What does it mean to command, if not to prepare the heart? In this way, with the inspiration of the Lord, that widow had her heart prepared to obey. The same Lord who was present in the woman also spoke with Elijah. The Lord was present in Elijah to command him and was present in the woman to obey him. Go, Elijah tells the woman, and give me first of your poverty; They will not diminish your wealth. The widow's entire estate consisted of a modest amount of flour and oil. And this small amount did not diminish. Who owns such a property? That widow fed the servant of God with great pleasure, since her assets were hanging by a nail. What is happier than this poverty? If here, on earth, you received such gifts, what gifts will you not expect in the end?

Using this rule, the Lord will help you elucidate and resolve many passages of Scripture, with which they weave the ties of their error. 3. Since it is not written that the devil saw God, but only that he appeared with the angels in the presence of the Lord and heard his voice, why do these wretches strive to slander the Scriptures and pervert the unlearned? His proposition is surpassed by a brief response. However great his loquacity may be to demonstrate that the devil saw God, we answer: The devil did not see God. They contradict: "How did you talk to him?" The blindness of their hearts must not be overcome by me, but by the experience of the blind themselves. Those who are blind in their carnal eyes can continually talk to those whom they cannot see. But how do they present themselves in his presence? they say. In the same way as the blind man in the presence of the one who sees, whom the blind man himself does not see. These similarities have been said, dear brothers, to reprove the perversity of carnal men and so that, seeing themselves thus repelled, they may turn their hearts towards the achievement of goodness. Can God, to whom all angelic and human consciousness is present, both good and bad, be contained in one place? It is interesting to note, however, that in good consciences He is present as Father, and in bad consciences as Judge, according to Scripture: The Lord challenges the just and the unjust. Just as it is written: God's interpellation will be in the thoughts of the

impious. And God's interpellation is no more intense in the ears of the body than in the secret of thought, where he only hears and is only heard. Do perverse men, when they say the truth, a certain thing, and are not believed, do they not swear and say: "God is a witness," and they say it with complete reason? Where is it a witness, I ask? In the tongue or in the heart? In the sound of the voice or in the loneliness of conscience? Where does the reason for their discomfort most of the time come from when they are not believed, and they realize that they are telling the truth, but because they cannot open their hearts to us where the witness is God? 4. There are many different ways in which God speaks to us. Sometimes He speaks to us through an instrument, as through the codex of the divine Scriptures. He speaks through some element of the world, as he spoke through the star of the wise men. What is locution, if it is not the manifestation of will? He speaks through luck, as in the case of Matthias putting him in the place of Judas. He speaks through the human soul, as through the prophet. He speaks through the angel, as to some of the patriarchs, prophets and apostles, as far as we know. He speaks through the noise of some creatures, as he spoke through the voices formed in the sky, without anyone seeing him. Finally, God speaks to man not only externally through the ears and eyes, but also internally and in various ways; He speaks in a dream, like to Laban the Syrian, so that he would not do harm to his servant Jacob; and to Pharaoh about seven years

Variis modis loquitur nobis Deus.—Multi autem modi sunt, quibus nobiscum loquitur Deus. Loquitur per sortem, sicut de Matthia in locum Iudae ordinando locutus est (Act 1,26): loquitur per animam humanom, sicut per prophetam: loquitur per angelum, sicut Patriarcharum et Prophetarum et Apostolorum quibusdam 'ocutum esse accipimus: loquitur per aliquam vocalem sonantemque creaturam, sicut de cáelo voz factas, cum oculis nullus víderetur, legimus et tenemus. On the contrary, they had no body, it was the same divine substance that was subject to the eyes of the devil. Which divine substance only those who have a pure heart see. Oh unscrupulous blindness of the heretics! Why do you falsely attribute to our Scriptures that the devil saw God and, denying the real body of Christ, do you strive to prove that the divine substance was contemplated by the devil? Or perhaps, as they say, Christ, not really having a human body, appeared as if he had one? Fools! Who feels more rightly and truthfully: the one who believes that God spoke with the devil or the one who believes that God not only spoke to the devil, but also lied to him? Scripture confirms that some angels appeared before the eyes of men. But certainly, in such a way the Lord subjected the corporeal creature to the power of the angels, that it accommodated itself to them according to his will. Hence, although not born of a woman, they truly had a real body, which they changed from one quality to another by virtue of their ministry and their office. We cannot say that the Lord himself, when he turned water into wine, used false water or false wine.

While many men cling to the defense that the entire corporeal nature does not come from the omnipotent God, but from I don't know what mob of darkness, we ask them: where did our Lord Jesus Christ take the body from? If they answer that he did not take a body, what was it that appeared before human and corporeal eyes? Or it was an invention of fantasy and believing it seems execrable; or if they strive to defend that their divine substance did not take the form of a body for human eyes, and this divine substance was what the devil saw, how can we understand what they proclaim with a slanderous voice: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God? If perhaps they say that the divine and proper substance of the Lord was not similar to that of the Father, as He wanted to manifest on earth without assuming any body, what do these wretches believe but that the divine substance is mutable and subject to times and places? Either they do not want to read or they cannot easily understand what is said in the prophet: You will change things and they will be changed; but you are always the same, and your years will have no end. And also what was written in the books of divine wisdom about wisdom itself: Remaining in itself, it renews all things. 11. Topic: Commentary on Psalm 2,10. Date: Around the year 418. Place: Carthage, in the Mensa Cypriani. 1. Teach all you who judge the earth. To judge the earth is to tame the body. Let us listen to the voice of the Apostle who judges the earth: I do not fight, he said, as one who whips the air, but I punish my body and reduce it to servitude, lest by preaching to others I myself become reprobate. CAPUT I.—1. Terram iudicare quid. Erudimini, omnes qui iudicatis terram.—Terram iudicare, est corpus domare. Audiamus Apostolum iudicantem terram: Non sic pugno, inquit, tanquam aerem caedens; sed punishment corpus meum et in servitutem redigo, ne forte alus praedicans ipse reprobus efficiar (1 Cor 4,26 et 27). Audi ergo, terra, iudicantem terram; et iudica terram, ne sis terra. Si enim terram iudicaveris, caelum eris, et in te factam gloriam Domini enarrabis. Caeli enim enarrant gloriam Dei (Ps 18:2). Si autem terram non iudicaveris, terra eris. Si autem terra fueris, ad eum pertinebis cui dictum est, Terram manducabis (Gen 3:14). Audiant ergo iudices terrae: corpus castigent, libídines frenent, ament sapientiam, vincant concupiscentiam: et ut hoc faciant, erudiantur.

2. The culmination of learning consists of the following: Serve the Lord with fear and exalt Him with trembling; exalt him, not yourself; to him by whom you are what you are; by which you are a man and you are just, if you are just. But if you judge that you are a man by him and that you are righteous by yourself, you do not serve the Lord with fear nor exalt him with trembling, but yourself with presumption. And what happens to you, except what follows?: So that the Lord will not be angry and you will deviate from the right path. It does not say: "Lest the Lord be angry and you enter the path of righteousness," but rather: you turn away from the righteous path. Therefore, if you judge yourself righteous because you do not steal, you do not commit adultery, you do not kill, you do not bear false witness against your neighbor, you honor father and mother, you worship one God, you do not serve idols and false gods; You will deviate from that path if you presume that all this is your doing and judge that all this is due to yourself. The unbelievers do not enter the right path, the proud turn away from it. Therefore it was said: Teach ye that judge the earth. And so that you do not attribute to yourselves the strength and power by which you judge the earth, so that you do not think that these virtues emanate from you, it is said: Serve the Lord with fear, exalt, not yourselves with presumption, but him with fear, so that the Lord will not be angry and you will turn from the right path when his anger is inflamed. What must we do to avoid deviating from the right path? Blessed are all those who trust in him. If those who trust in him are blessed,

Those who trust in themselves are miserable. Cursed is every man who puts his hope in man; then not even in yourself, since you are also a man. If you put your hope in another man, you would be inordinately humble; If you put it in you, you would be dangerously arrogant. What is the right thing to do? Both things are harmful. Don't choose any of them; for he who is humble in an inordinate manner will not be exalted; and he who is dangerously arrogant will be destroyed. 3. Finally, that your holiness may recognize in what sense each person's self-confidence must be destroyed and rejected, these words were spoken: Serve the Lord with fear and exalt him with trembling. Listen to the Apostle, who says these words and who explains this sentence in this way. Here are his words: Work out your salvation with fear and trembling. "Why should I work for my salvation with fear and trembling, if it is in my power to obtain it?" Do you want to hear why with fear and trembling? God is the one who works in you. That is why you must work with fear and trembling, because what the humble achieves, the proud loses. But if it is God who works in you, why has it been said: Work out your salvation yourselves? Because he works in us in such a way that we also work. Be my help. Such an expression designates that he who invokes help, he himself works. "My will is good," he says. I confess that it is yours. But by whom has it been given to you, who has excited it in you? Don't listen to me,

Exsulta ei, non tibí: ei a quo es quod es, et quod homo es, et quod iustus es; if tamen iam iustus is. Si autem putaveris quod ab illo quidem homo es, a te autem iustus es; do not serve Domino in timore, nec exsultas ei in tremore, sed tibi in praesumptione. Et quid tibi fiet, nisi quod sequitur? Ne quando irascatur Dominus, et pereatis, inquit, de via iusta. Non enim ait, Ne quando irascatur Dominus, et non intretis in viam iustam; sed pereatis de via iusta. Iam enim videris tibi iustus non rapiendo alienum, non adulterando, non homicidium fazando, non falsum testimonium adversus proximum dicendo, patrem et matrem honorando, unum Deum colendo, idolis et daemoniis non serviendo: de hac via peribis, si tibi ista praesumpseris, si tibi ista a te ipso esse putaveris. Infideles enim non intrant in viam iustam, superbi pereunt de via iusta. Quid enim ait? Erudimini, omnes qui iudicatis terram. Et ne forte vires et potentiam, qua iudicatis terram, vobis tribuatis, et a vobis ipsis eam vobis esse credatis; nolite sic: Servite Domino in timore; exsultate, non vobis in praesumptione, sed ei in tremore. Ne quando irascatur Dominus, et pereatis de via iusta, cum exarserit cita ira eius. Quid ergo faciendum est, ne pereamus de via iusta? Beati omnes qui confidunt in eum (Ps 11,10-13). Si beati qui confidunt in eum; miseri qui confidunt in se.
